# Phase 28 — NextSQL Admin (Setup + Operations modes)

NextSQL must be easy to install and operate without sacrificing headless automation or secure defaults.

## Product shape

NextSQL Admin is one application (`nextsql-admin`), one frontend shell, three modes:

```text
Setup mode       → install / upgrade / repair / uninstall           (this phase)
Operations mode  → server / cluster / security / backup / operations (this phase)
Studio mode      → database development / SQL / data / schema        (Phase 29)
```

This phase (28) covers Setup and Operations mode. Phase 29 covers Studio mode, built
inside the same shell rather than as a separate binary — see that phase's "Product shape"
note.

## Installer platforms

- [ ] Windows `Setup.exe` — `scripts/build-windows-installer.sh` cross-compiles a self-extracting setup stub; execution unverified, no Wine/Windows host in this environment (log #134)
- [ ] Windows MSI if justified
- [x] Linux `.deb` — `scripts/build-linux-installer.sh` builds it (`fakeroot dpkg-deb`); control/maintainer-scripts/file layout verified with `dpkg-deb --info`/`--contents`; live system-wide `dpkg -i` untested (would mutate this shared host) (log #134)
- [x] Linux `.rpm` — built and live-installed end to end via `dnf install` on `fedora:40` (rpmbuild not available on this host directly; used Docker); two real `nextsql.spec.in` bugs found and fixed along the way (relative `%doc`/`%license` paths, missing `nextsql-admin`/`USAGE.md.gz`/`VERSION` in `%files`) (log #143)
- [x] Linux `.tar.gz` — build + `--user` install → `nextsql init` → real `nextsqld` → `nextsql exec` → `uninstall.sh` verified end to end (log #134); now also bundles `nextsql-install` as the default interactive entry point (`--user` mode, TTY-gated), live-verified through a real Chrome browser end to end including a real systemd `enable --now` (log #140)
- [x] Linux `.run` — self-extracting stub verified: extracts and runs `install.sh` correctly, installed binary runs (log #134); same `nextsql-install` bundling as `.tar.gz` (log #140)
- [ ] macOS `.pkg`/`.dmg` only when tested/supported
- [x] OCI/container non-interactive initialization — `nextsql-entrypoint` (`internal/dockerentry`) drives `nextsql setup` on first start from env (`NEXTSQL_PROFILE` developer/production, `NEXTSQL_PRESET`, `NEXTSQL_SERVER_USER`/password, TLS), writes `nextsql.conf` into the data volume, and passes it to `nextsqld` with `--config` on every start so the deployment profile + production preflight persist; production fails closed on a missing admin / key-on-data-volume / non-loopback-without-TLS (log #216)
- [x] Silent/non-interactive installation — `install.sh`'s existing non-interactive default path (no TTY, or `--no-gui`, or `--system`/root) is confirmed byte-for-byte unchanged by the GUI-installer bundling (log #140); full unattended coverage now live-verified end to end for `.tar.gz`/`.run` (isolated `HOME`/XDG env, zero prompts, `nextsql setup --json` → real server → real query → `uninstall.sh`) and `.deb` (`DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install` in a disposable container) (log #143)
- [x] Signed release/checksum pipeline — `SHA256SUMS*` are produced and verify (`sha256sum -c`, log #134); `--gpg-key ID` (or `NEXTSQL_RELEASE_GPG_KEY`) on both `scripts/build-{linux,windows}-installer.sh` now detached-signs the checksums file via a shared `sign_checksums` helper (`packaging/lib.sh`) — opt-in (no signing key exists in this repo/CI yet, matching every other optional-tool tolerance in these scripts), but once a key is given, a missing `gpg` or a signing failure aborts the build rather than silently shipping unsigned artifacts. Verified live with a throwaway test key: good signature verifies, a tampered `SHA256SUMS.linux` correctly fails verification, no key given produces no `.asc` (log #144)

## Installer UX

- [x] Modern welcome screen with version/architecture/channel — `nextsql-install`'s Welcome step shows version/phase/OS/elevation (log #135); no "channel" concept exists in this repo (single rolling pre-1.0 line), so that part is N/A rather than done
- [x] Standard vs Advanced installation — the Resources step's "Advanced" toggle switches to `nextsql setup --skip-init` (write the config only, don't initialize a database now), skipping the Administrator step since it would have no effect (log #136)
- [x] Component selection — NextSQL has no optional install components (single engine, single binary); `docs/design-installer-gui.md` M3 treats this line as the wizard's advanced-options surface (skip-init, custom buffer pages, remote listen + TLS), all three of which are now landed (M1 logs #135/#136, remote listen + TLS log #138)
- [x] Data-directory picker + capacity/permission validation — the Location step's "Check" (and auto-check on Continue) runs `nextsql setup --dry-run` live and renders disk free/total + warnings before anything is written (log #135); permission errors surface as the real error from the dry run rather than a separate pre-flight
- [x] Secure encryption setup wizard — the Location step explains the key file's role (log #135) and now (log #137) shows, before anything is written, exactly what will happen at the path typed in: "new key will be generated" or "existing key will be imported and reused", refreshed on every `Check` and repeated on the Review step right before confirmation
- [x] Generate/import root unlock key — the choice was always available (point the key-file field at a fresh path to generate, or an existing one to import — `nextsql init` has always imported a pre-existing file as-is and only generates when the path is empty) but silent; log #137 makes it explicit via `nextsql setup`'s new `key_file_exists`/`instance_key_exists` `--json` fields + matching advisory text, surfaced in the GUI as an explicit banner rather than left implicit. Not a separate radio/toggle control — the path field itself is the choice, same as the CLI; recovery-key export/verification in the wizard closed the rest of M2 in log #243
- [x] Default root-key path separated from data volume — `internal/installgui.detectDefaults` suggests the same split `packaging/linux/tarball/install.sh` uses (key under `/etc`/`~/.config`, data under `/var/lib`/`~/.local/share`) (log #135)
- [x] Recovery-key export/verification UX — the capability landed in log #242 (a second, independent AES-256 key sealing the same KEK, `NSKS` keystore v2, `nextsql key add-recovery` / `verify-recovery` / `remove-recovery` / `recover` for both the database and deployment-registry keystores); the install-time half landed in log #243: `nextsql setup --recovery-key-out FILE` generates, seals and double-verifies one for **each** keystore inside the install's rollback boundary, and the Setup wizard offers it on by default, names both export paths before anything is written, withdraws it when "configuration only" is chosen, and holds Finish until the operator confirms both files were copied offline. Verified live end to end with both root key files deleted. See `docs/security.md` "Recovery keys"
- [x] Never upload root key — the password/key never leave loopback: the browser posts it once to `nextsql-install`'s own local API, which writes it to a mode-0600 temp file for one subprocess call and deletes it immediately after (log #135, `internal/installgui/runner.go`)
- [x] Administrator account creation — the Administrator step (log #135)
- [x] Password strength/visibility/validation UX — client-side strength hint, a "Show passwords" toggle, and a mismatch/minimum-length gate before Continue (log #135)
- [x] Loopback-only network default (`127.0.0.1:7210`) — `nextsql setup` (log #104); the Resources step's listen-address field is blank/hidden by default (an explicit second "Advanced" checkbox reveals it), so every GUI install stays loopback unless the operator opts in (log #135, extended log #138)
- [x] Remote-listen flow requires TLS — `nextsql setup` rejects a non-loopback `--listen` without `--tls-cert`/`--tls-key`, exit 6, writes nothing (log #104); now reachable from the GUI (log #138) — the Resources step's network fields feed straight into `--listen`/`--tls-cert`/`--tls-key`, and the CLI's rejection is the one authoritative check, surfaced through the existing plan-error banner
- [x] TLS certificate assistant and validation — the Resources step's "configure a remote listen address" section (log #138): listen-address + TLS certificate/private-key path fields (paths only, never uploaded — same contract as the root key file), a client-side non-loopback hint before Continue, and `nextsql setup --dry-run`'s existing check as the authoritative validator. Not a certificate *generator* or a client-side cert-content inspector (matching-key/expiry/SAN checks) — the operator supplies an already-issued cert/key pair, same as the CLI
- [ ] Optional explicit firewall-rule creation
- [x] Hardware detection (CPU/RAM/disk/filesystem) — `internal/sysinfo`, full on Linux; RAM/filesystem undetected (reported as such) on other platforms (log #104); surfaced live in the GUI's Location/Resources steps (log #135)
- [x] Balanced / Memory Conservative / High Performance / Custom resource presets — `nextsql setup --preset`, buffer pool = 10/25/50% of detected RAM (log #104); the Resources step exposes all four with a live buffer-pool preview (log #135)
- [x] Installation summary before mutation — `nextsql setup --dry-run` covers the CLI path (log #104); the GUI's Summary step renders every field Install will use, built from the exact same `Params` the dry-run call used, before the one mutating `/api/v1/install` call (log #135)
- [ ] Meaningful staged progress — a single spinner during the one blocking `nextsql setup` call, not per-step progress (`nextsql setup` has no streaming protocol to report sub-steps yet)
- [x] Transactional rollback of safe installer changes — `nextsql setup` (log #110); the GUI drives that exact command as a subprocess, so a failed GUI install rolls back identically (log #135)
- [x] Never delete existing user data/keys on failed install — same reasoning: the GUI never touches the filesystem itself, only through `nextsql setup`'s already-verified rollback (logs #106–#108, #110, #135)
- [x] Automatic post-install health verification — `nextsql setup` runs header-compat + engine-open check, exit 5 on failure (log #104); the GUI's completion screen surfaces the `health` result (log #135)
- [x] Completion screen with safe connection settings — shows the `nextsqld --data-dir/--key-file/--listen` command to run next (or, for a skip-init install, the `nextsql setup --config-in` command to finish it later); never echoes the password (log #135); a "Finish" button now ends the installer process itself via `POST /api/v1/finish`, so a GUI-only operator never needs to switch to a terminal and press Ctrl+C (log #136)
- [x] No root key/password in connection strings — the completion screen's connection snippet has neither (log #135)
- [x] Service registration / start automatically at boot — M6 (`PROJECT.md` §46 "service registration", log #139): an optional Resources-step checkbox that, after a successful install, runs `systemctl [--user] enable --now nextsql` — but only against a "nextsql" unit already installed on this host (by a packaged `.deb`/`.tar.gz`/`.run` installer) whose own `--config` already matches the configuration this run just wrote. The wizard never authors a unit file itself (that stays the packaged installer's job — `packaging/linux/nextsql.service`); on any host with no matching unit it's shown disabled with a clear reason, never silently ignored. New `internal/installgui/service.go` (`DetectService`/`EnableService`/`WaitActive`, the only place besides `nextsql setup` this package shells out from) + `GET /api/v1/service` + `Params.EnableService`. Distinguishes "enabled to start at boot" from "actually running now" (`enabled`/`active` fields) — a real bug found live during verification: `systemctl enable --now` exits 0 once a start is *issued*, even for a unit whose process exits immediately after, so the first cut would have falsely reported success; fixed with a bounded (~1.5s, 4 attempts) `WaitActive` re-check after enabling
- [x] Developer setup preset — `--profile developer` (CLI default): loopback-friendly, skip-init allowed, administrator optional, resource presets unchanged (log #208)
- [x] Production setup preset — `--profile production` / Setup-mode GUI default: writes `deployment_profile=production` plus disk-watermark, replica-lag, drain, statement/idle/lock timeout, and connection-limit defaults; GUI requires an administrator and disables skip-init (log #208)
- [x] Production security preflight — fail-closed at `nextsql setup` (no skip-init, unlock key off the data volume, administrator required on a real install) and again at `nextsqld` start when `deployment_profile=production` or `--production`; tmpfs/ramfs is a warning (log #208)
- [x] Light/dark/system UI — explicit persisted three-state selector shared with Manager; `system` follows `prefers-color-scheme` and remains selectable after a fixed override (log #141)
- [x] Keyboard/screen-reader/high-contrast accessibility — semantic progress/current-step state, skip link, focus + live announcements for every view transition, labelled/error-associated form controls, keyboard combobox navigation, reduced-motion and increased/forced-contrast CSS; real headless-Chrome keyboard flow + axe WCAG 2.2 A/AA audit green for Installer and the visually aligned Manager shell (log #141)
- [x] Actionable error messages — a failed plan/install now leads with a first-run-audience headline + next step (`explainSetupError`/`SetupErrorAlert`, `src/setup/`), with `nextsql setup`'s verbatim text kept one "Technical details" disclosure away (expanded automatically when unrecognized). Covers non-loopback-without-TLS, existing config/database, production profile missing an admin/key/resource-policy setting, key on the data volume, unwritable paths, full disk, failed health check, missing binary; anything else falls back to a generic message with the raw text shown. Presentation only — no API surface, no outcome change; `npm run test:setup` (log #217)
- [x] Protected installer logs with secret redaction — `nextsql-install`'s own request log records only method/path/status/duration, never a request body, the token, or subprocess stdout/stderr (log #135)

## Installer lifecycle

- [x] Detect existing installation — `nextsql lifecycle detect` (log #105): config/database/keystore presence, resolved paths, header compatibility, deployment-lock (server-running) probe → one status; Setup mode now exposes the same **read-only** inspect action at the selected data/config paths (`POST /api/v1/lifecycle/detect`), before a fresh install is attempted. Upgrade/repair/uninstall remain explicit CLI flows pending their own confirmation UX.
- [x] Upgrade mode — `nextsql lifecycle upgrade` (log #106): hold the deployment lock for the whole operation → preflight → verified config backup → open the encrypted store once with this binary (runs WAL recovery, confirms the catalog decodes under the new format code) → re-verify headers. Outcomes `applied` / `dry-run` / `blocked` (2/6/7) / `failed-verify` (5). Never deletes anything; does not swap the binary or restart a service (the OS installer does that around this call). Rolling-cluster integration landed as log #118 (`--cluster-node` acknowledgment + printed per-node procedure). GUI surface still pending
- [x] Repair mode — `nextsql lifecycle repair` (log #108): regenerates a missing/unparseable `nextsql.conf` (unparseable → backed up first; parseable → untouched unless `--force-config`) with secure defaults; reports config/key-file permission drift and tightens it with `--fix-perms` (never loosens); opens the encrypted store once (runs WAL recovery) to confirm health. Preserves the database + keys always. Outcomes `repaired`/`healthy`/`dry-run`/`blocked` (2/7)/`failed` (5); refuses while a server holds the lock; not `setup` (won't initialize). GUI surface pending
- [x] Uninstall mode — `nextsql lifecycle uninstall` (log #107): removes only `nextsql.conf` + `.bak-*` by default; `--purge-data` also removes the primary DB + sidecars + auth/ACL/audit + deployment-registry DB + lock; `--purge-keys` (requires `--purge-data` + resolvable key paths) also removes the external key files; dry run until `--confirm`; blocked while a server holds the lock (exit 2) or on inconsistent flags (exit 6). Outcomes `planned`/`removed`/`blocked`/`partial`. GUI surface pending
- [x] Upgrade preflight for storage/catalog/protocol compatibility — `nextsql lifecycle preflight` (log #105): keyless superblock/WAL-control/UNDO-control/envelope header versions vs `internal/upgrade/compat`, verdict + exit code (0/2/6/7); catalog/protocol compat inside the encrypted store is still enforced at server start
- [x] Config backup before upgrade — `nextsql lifecycle backup-config` (log #105): timestamped `nextsql.conf.bak-<UTC>`, mode 0640, reload-and-compare verified
- [x] Rolling-cluster upgrade integration — `nextsql lifecycle upgrade` (log #118) detects Raft membership offline (a `raft/` state dir, the key-free `nextsql.cluster.json` status file, or `node_id`+`raft_bind` in the config) and refuses to mutate the node until `--cluster-node` acknowledges it has been drained (and leadership transferred if it was the leader) — outcome `blocked` (exit 6) otherwise, with the ordered per-node procedure printed. `--dry-run` and `nextsql lifecycle detect` show the same procedure without the gate; the `--json` output carries it under `rolling_upgrade` for an installer/Manager to drive. New pure `internal/setup.PlanRollingUpgrade`/`RollingStep`/`ClusterUpgradeGuidance`. The offline per-node upgrade itself is unchanged (WAL recovery only; Raft log replays on restart) — the flag is a sequencing acknowledgment, not a technical barrier. `docs/ops.md` "Rolling upgrade" step 3 + `docs/install.md` updated
- [x] Repair preserves data/keys/config unless explicitly approved — `nextsql lifecycle repair` never touches the database or unlock key contents; a parseable config is left as-is unless `--force-config`, permissions are only changed with `--fix-perms` and only tightened (log #108)
- [x] Uninstall preserves data and keys by default — `nextsql lifecycle uninstall` keeps the database and the external unlock keys unless `--purge-data` / `--purge-keys` is explicitly given (log #107)
- [x] Dangerous deletion choices disabled by default — every `uninstall` run is a dry run until `--confirm`; `--purge-keys` requires `--purge-data` (and resolvable key paths) or the run is blocked with nothing deleted (log #107)

## Automation parity

- [x] Every GUI-installer option maps to CLI/config automation — `/plan` and `/install` build the same bounded `Params` and drive `nextsql setup`; M3/M4-Linux/M5/M6 are landed, while M2 recovery-key UX and non-Linux M4 packaging remain explicitly gated (logs #135–#141)
- [x] `nextsql setup` or equivalent — non-interactive detect → plan → config → init → verify (log #104, `docs/install.md`)
- [x] Non-interactive exit codes — `nextsql setup` uses the shared `internal/cli` scheme (0 ok / 1 flag / 5 health / 6 validation / 7 missing-required) (log #104)
- [x] Machine-readable output — `nextsql setup --json` emits one object: hardware, sizing decision + rationale, resolved paths, init/health result, warnings (log #104)
- [x] Config-file-driven install — `--config-in FILE` seeds defaults, `--config-out FILE` targets the generated `nextsql.conf`; `config.Config.Marshal` round-trips with `config.Load` (log #104)
- [x] Non-interactive install-detection / preflight / config-backup / in-place-upgrade automation — `nextsql lifecycle detect|preflight|backup-config|upgrade`, all `--json` (logs #105, #106)
- [x] Offline installation supported — verified live, not just by absent-network-call inspection: full `install.sh --system --no-gui` → `nextsql setup --json` → `nextsqld` → real `nextsql exec … SELECT 1`, and separately `nextsql-admin`'s Setup-mode wizard serving its first page, all inside a `docker run --network none` container (log #144)
- [x] No mandatory cloud login/activation/telemetry — repo-wide grep for outbound `net/http` clients, `curl`/`wget`, or any `http://`/`https://` reference across `internal/setup`, `internal/admin/setup`, `cmd/nextsql`, and every `packaging/linux/*` script found none; the only `net/http` usage in the setup path is the wizard's own local loopback server (log #144)

## Operations mode MVP (formerly "NextSQL Manager")

**Renamed 2026-09-05 (log #142)**: `nextsql-manager`/`internal/manager` became
`nextsql-admin`/`internal/admin/ops` — one mode of the unified NextSQL Admin binary
alongside Setup mode (formerly the separate Installer) and the new Studio-mode
placeholder. Behavior, routes, and the M1-M9 slice history below are unchanged; only the
binary/package names and design-doc location (`docs/design-admin.md`, superseding
`docs/design-manager.md`) moved. See log #142 for the restructuring itself.

**Architecture chosen 2026-09-04 (`AskUserQuestion`): a local web app served
by Go** — a single `nextsql-manager` binary serves an embedded static UI plus
a JSON API over a loopback HTTP listener; the operator opens it in their
browser. Rejected Electron (size / attack surface — `PROJECT.md`'s explicit
caution), Wails (per-OS webview dependency + JS build step for a marginal
gain), Fyne (weak accessibility for dense tables). Full rationale and the
M1–M9 slice decomposition: **`docs/design-manager.md`**.

**M1 landed 2026-09-04 (log #119): serving backbone + Overview.** The
`nextsql-manager` binary + `internal/manager` package: loopback HTTP server
(non-loopback `--listen` requires `--tls-cert`/`--tls-key`), an embedded
shell, session/auth/CSRF layer (operator logs in with their own NSQL
credentials → the Manager opens a driver connection as that user → bounded,
self-expiring in-memory session + `SameSite=Strict` cookie + per-session CSRF
token on state-changing calls; no Manager service account, no key access, no
engine-package imports), and `GET /api/v1/overview` (server `system.storage` /
`system.replication` state, live session & active-query counts, the
capability registry).

**M2 (Databases & Storage) + M3 (Connections & Activity) landed 2026-09-04
(log #120)**: `GET /api/v1/databases` (`system.storage`, `system.databases` /
`system.realms` with a `hosted` flag — empty-and-reported, not errored, on a
single-database deployment — `system.tables`, `system.table_stats`) and
`GET /api/v1/activity` (`system.sessions`, `system.active_queries`,
`system.transactions`, `system.locks`). Both share the new `runBundle`
read-model helper with M1's Overview (a named set of `system.*` queries; a
non-required query that errors becomes a warning + empty result rather than
failing the whole view). **Scope correction from the original plan**:
"Query cancellation using existing engine path" assumed a server-side
cancel-another-session surface that does not exist — NextSQL cancellation is
client-driven (cancel your own connection's context) or credential-driven
(`nextsql token revoke`); M3 is therefore observe-only, and cancellation (if
it lands) belongs with credential revocation under M4 Security.

**Frontend rebuilt on React + `@bzync/rui` 2026-09-04 (log #121)**, replacing
M1's hand-written vanilla-JS shell — decided via `AskUserQuestion` ("adopt
now" over "adopt at M4" or "stay vanilla"): M4–M9 need real forms/dialogs/data
tables where a component library pays for itself, and `@bzync/rui` keeps the
Manager visually consistent with `docs/web` (the product site), which already
uses it. New `internal/manager/frontend/` (a standalone npm package, esbuild
bundle) is the source; the bundled `app.js`/`app.css` it emits into
`internal/manager/web/` is committed, so `go build ./...` still needs no Node
toolchain. Full stack rationale + structure: `docs/design-manager.md` §1
"Frontend stack". M4–M9 subsequently landed and the Manager MVP exit gate is
closed (logs #122–#133) — see the design doc and the checked status below.

- [x] Server overview/status — `GET /api/v1/overview` + the Overview view (M1, log #119); process start/stop/restart stays out of MVP scope (needs the privileged helper)
- [ ] Start/stop/restart — needs the separate minimal privileged helper (`PROJECT.md` §47); explicitly out of MVP scope
- [x] Graceful restart/drain integration — `POST /api/v1/cluster/action` `drain` (M6, log #123) issues `CLUSTER DRAIN [WITH (TIMEOUT_MS = n)]`; **verified live**: this stops accepting connections then exits the `nextsqld` process entirely (not just this session) — the Manager cannot itself restart it (needs the same privileged helper as "Start/stop/restart" above), so the Cluster view's confirmation dialog says so explicitly
- [x] Configuration viewer — `GET /api/v1/config` + the Configuration view (M8, log #127; write path added log #132): `system.config`, one row per non-default `config.Config` / `nextsql.conf` setting with `value`/`file_value`/`restart_required`, every network-address-shaped value redacted. Admin-only; zero rows for embedded/CLI use.
- [x] Safe configuration editor + validation — new `SET CONFIG key = value` statement (M8, log #132): cluster `ADMIN`, node-local, persist-only to the node's `nextsql.conf` through the server (client never touches a path); `config.WithSetting` validates/range-checks the value exactly as `config.Load` would, then `Validate()`s. `POST /api/v1/config/action` + an inline per-row editor in the Configuration view (key allowlisted against `config.SettableKeys()` before interpolation; value always a quoted literal). Fails `Unavailable` if `nextsqld` was started without `--config`. Audited `config.set`.
- [x] Restart-required indicators — `system.config` gained `file_value` + `restart_required` columns (`config.DiffState`, M8 log #132): every `SET CONFIG` write is persist-only, so a changed key reads `restart_required=yes` (running value vs on-disk value) until `nextsqld` restarts; also surfaces a startup flag that overrode the file. The Configuration view shows a "restart required" badge per row.
- [x] Database listing/size — `GET /api/v1/databases` + the Databases view (M2, log #120): `system.storage`/`system.databases`/`system.realms`/`system.tables`/`system.table_stats`
- [x] Connection information — `GET /api/v1/activity` + the Activity view (M3, log #120): `system.sessions`
- [x] Users/roles/privileges viewer — `GET /api/v1/security` + the Security view (M4, log #122): `system.users`/`system.roles`/`system.grants` (admin-only server-side, empty not error for a non-admin, same as the underlying tables); mutation (`CREATE USER`/`GRANT`/`REVOKE` forms) is not wired yet, still open
- [ ] Security dashboard
- [x] Key-rotation status (read-only, no display of keys) — `system.key_versions` + the Security view's "Key rotation" table (M4, log #126): current version + retained/revoked/retired counts per key (`kek`, `master`, and each data domain), no key material anywhere in the returned type. Admin-only; zero rows (list-shaped, not a placeholder row) when no persistent envelope is attached. Wired only onto the legacy/non-hosted `db`/`env` (same scope `SetDrainFunc`/`SetTLSStatusSource` already have) — see `docs/design-manager.md` M4. "Action" (triggering a rotation from the Manager) is still open — this is status/read-only.
- [x] TLS status/configuration (read-only) — `system.tls` + the Security view's `TLSStatusCard` (M4, log #125): subject/issuer/validity/DNS SANs/mTLS/CRL posture, no key material or network address, admin-only, always one row (`enabled=false` when no listener attached). Wired only onto the legacy/non-hosted `db` (same scope `SetDrainFunc` already has) — a hosted-mode session's `system.tls` doesn't yet reflect the process listener's real TLS state, see `docs/design-manager.md` M4. Configuration (editing TLS settings) is still open — this is status/read-only.
- [x] Audit viewer — `system.audit_verify` (chain-integrity status, one row) + `system.audit_log` (bounded 200-row tail) + the Security view's `AuditVerifyCard`/"Audit log" table (M4, log #128): new `security.TailEvents`, extending the existing `security.VerifyFile` streaming scanner; live-verified to correctly detect an externally-tampered file on the very next query, with no restart, and to still surface the suspect record rather than hide it. Admin-only, no secrets ever in scope (`Event`'s own write-time contract). This closes M4's originally scoped surface (users/roles/grants + TLS status + key-rotation status + audit viewer, logs #122/#125/#126/#128).
- [x] Backup creation — `BACKUP DATABASE` statement + `POST /api/v1/backups/action` `{op:"create"}` + the Backups view's "Back up now" button (M5, log #133). New `backup.CreateFromEngine` hot-backup path: reuses the server's already-open engine (checkpoint → fuzzy copy → WAL-replay reconciliation on restore), no second `storage.Open`/recovery. Writes into a timestamped subdir of config key `backup_dir`; `BACKUP` privilege or cluster `ADMIN`; fails `Unavailable` if `backup_dir` unset.
- [x] Backup verification status — `VERIFY BACKUP 'name'` statement + per-row Verify action (M5, log #133): hash verification + restore test into a temp dir, never touches the live data file; surfaces `verified`/`problem`. `system.backups` lists the backups.
- [ ] Restore/PITR UI — **deliberately out of MVP scope** (M5, log #133): a running server cannot restore into itself (same inherent limit as M6's `DRAIN` exiting the process), so restore/PITR stays `nextsql restore` CLI; the Backups view prints the exact command with the right flags.
- [ ] Cluster creation wizard — needs the privileged helper + installer integration; explicitly out of MVP scope
- [x] Cluster dashboard — `GET /api/v1/cluster` + the Cluster view (M6, log #123): `system.replication` + `system.replica_health`
- [x] Quorum/leader/follower/lag display — same read-model as above (`voters`/`has_leader`/`applied_lsn` from `system.replication`; `role`/`apply_backlog`/`last_contact_ms`/`healthy` from `system.replica_health`)
- [x] Maintenance UI — `GET /api/v1/maintenance` + `POST /api/v1/maintenance/action` + the Maintenance view (M7, log #124): `system.tables`/`system.indexes`/`system.table_stats`/`system.index_stats`, plus `ANALYZE`/`REBUILD INDEX [ONLINE]`/`MAINTAIN DATABASE|TABLE|INDEX`, each behind a confirmation dialog
- [x] Index rebuild UI — `REBUILD INDEX name [ONLINE]` via the same Maintenance view/action endpoint (M7, log #124)
- [x] Storage reclamation UI — `MAINTAIN DATABASE|TABLE|INDEX` via the same Maintenance view/action endpoint (M7, log #124); capped at 10,000 tombstones per statement server-side, not a progress-tracked long-running job
- [x] Statistics refresh UI — `ANALYZE [table]` via the same Maintenance view/action endpoint (M7, log #124); live-verified `system.table_stats.row_count` updates in the very next read after running it
- [x] Performance metrics — `GET /api/v1/diagnostics` + the Diagnostics view (M9, log #129): `system.metrics`, one row per counter/gauge in the process-wide `metrics.Snapshot` (throughput/latency/encryption/storage/replication/constraints/maintenance/cdc/runtime), sourced via `executor.DB.SetMetricsSource`. `nextsqld` also routes the connected DB's own query/txn counters into `metrics.Default()` (`SetMetrics`) so one snapshot is internally coherent. Admin-only; zero rows for embedded/CLI use. Same legacy/non-hosted `db` wiring-scope caveat as `system.tls`/`system.config`.
- [x] Active queries — `GET /api/v1/activity` + the Activity view (M3, log #120): `system.active_queries`
- [ ] Query cancellation using existing engine path — scope-corrected (M3, log #120): NextSQL has no server-side cancel-another-session surface; cancellation is client-driven or credential-driven (`nextsql token revoke`) — see `docs/design-manager.md` §6 M3
- [x] Logs/diagnostics — metrics panel (M9, log #129, `system.metrics`) + server-log tail (M9, log #130, `system.server_log` over a new bounded `internal/logging.Ring` wired via `logging.NewWithRing`) + `GET /api/v1/diagnostics` read-model + Diagnostics view/tab (log #131 completes M9)
- [x] Redacted diagnostic bundle export — `GET /api/v1/diagnostics/bundle` (M9, log #131): one indented JSON attachment assembled entirely from admin-only `system.*` read surfaces (`metrics`/`server_log`/`config`/`capabilities`/`storage`/`replication`/`replica_health`/`tls`/`key_versions`/`audit_verify` — chain status only, never log content). Every constituent already redacted at its source; a top-level `note` field states what is and isn't included; no tenant row data. Driver-only, no data-directory access.
- [x] Destructive-action confirmations — Cluster (M6), Maintenance (M7), Configuration writes (M8), and Backup creation/verification (M5) require an explicit `@bzync/rui` `ConfirmDialog` before firing (logs #123, #124, #132, #133)

## UI architecture

- [x] Operations mode uses official NSQL/system interfaces — every query goes through `drivers/go` against `nextsqld` as the operator's own NSQL user (M1, log #119); no private code path
- [x] No direct page/WAL/catalog manipulation — `internal/admin/ops` (formerly `internal/manager`) imports none of `internal/storage`/`wal`/`catalog`/`crypto`/`recovery`; enforced by an `imports_test.go` boundary test (M1, log #119; ported log #142)
- [ ] Minimal privileged helper for OS-only tasks — deferred with process start/stop; not part of the MVP
- [x] Operations mode does not run permanently as root/Administrator — `nextsql-admin` (formerly `nextsql-manager`) is an unprivileged HTTP process with no key/data-dir access and no service account (M1, log #119)
- [x] UI framework evaluated for security/performance/accessibility/size/offline support — `docs/design-admin.md` (formerly `docs/design-manager.md`) §1 comparison table (local web app vs Wails vs Fyne vs Electron)
- [x] Do not choose Electron automatically; justify framework — Electron rejected on size + attack surface; local-web-app chosen and justified in `docs/design-admin.md` §1 (log #119)

- [ ] Fresh Windows install tested
- [x] Fresh Linux install tested — live amd64 `.tar.gz` and `.run` install/init/start/query/uninstall flows passed; `.deb` metadata/layout was inspected but not installed system-wide (log #134); the GUI-installer-bundled `--user` interactive flow additionally verified end to end through a real Chrome browser, including a real systemd unit enable (log #140)
- [x] Secure defaults generated — `nextsql setup` unit/integration/live coverage (logs #104, #110, #135)
- [x] Service initializes/starts/verifies — live Linux tarball/run and GUI-API flows (logs #134, #135)
- [x] Remote plaintext blocked — setup rejects non-loopback listen without TLS before mutation (log #104)
- [x] Secret material absent from logs — password-file boundary and request-log tests cover GUI M1; live outputs contain no password/key (log #135)
- [x] Silent install tested — `.tar.gz`/`.run` (isolated scratch `HOME`, zero prompts) and `.deb` (`apt-get install -y` noninteractive in a disposable container), each end to end through a real query (log #143)
- [x] Upgrade tested — `nextsql lifecycle upgrade` has unit + live coverage (logs #106, #118 — #118 adds the rolling-cluster `--cluster-node` gate); the end-to-end installer path now verified using the actual packaged `.tar.gz` binaries (`--dry-run` then real, `applied`, engine reopened cleanly, post-upgrade query succeeded) (log #143)
- [x] Repair tested — `nextsql lifecycle repair` has unit + live coverage (log #108); the end-to-end installer path now verified using the actual packaged `.tar.gz` binaries (missing config regenerated, engine health-verified, data intact, post-repair query succeeded) (log #143)
- [x] Uninstall preserves data/keys by default — enforced by `nextsql lifecycle uninstall` and confirmed by the live Linux tarball uninstall flow (logs #107, #134)
- [x] Failure rollback tested — `nextsql setup` transactional rollback has unit/live coverage and GUI M1 delegates to that exact subprocess path; runner failure cases are covered (logs #110, #135)
- [x] Accessibility baseline passes — deterministic Chrome keyboard walkthrough + axe WCAG 2.2 A/AA audit covers all installer views (welcome through finished), explicit theme states, semantic focus/announcements, path-combobox interaction, password confirmation, and emulated increased-contrast/reduced-motion behavior; the aligned Manager login/overview/databases shell passes the same audit (log #141)

### Phase 28 Operations-mode exit gate (formerly "Manager exit gate")

- [x] Operations mode can perform its MVP operations through official interfaces — **all nine slices landed**: M1–M3 (Overview, Databases, Activity), M4 (Security — users/roles/grants + TLS/key-rotation status + audit viewer), M5 (Backups — `BACKUP DATABASE` / `VERIFY BACKUP` / `system.backups`; restore/PITR deliberately CLI-only), M6 (Cluster + actions), M7 (Maintenance + actions), M8 (Configuration viewer + `SET CONFIG` editor), M9 (metrics + server-log tail + diagnostic-bundle export). Every mutating operation is a documented SQL statement issued on the operator's own connection (logs #119–#133)
- [x] RBAC enforced server-side — structurally true from M1 (every op runs as the operator's own NSQL user; Operations mode has no service account) and re-confirmed per slice: M4 tables are admin-only server-side; M5 `BACKUP DATABASE`/`VERIFY BACKUP` require the `BACKUP` privilege or cluster `ADMIN`; M6 `CLUSTER …` actions require `ADMIN ON CLUSTER`; M7 `ANALYZE`/`REBUILD INDEX`/`MAINTAIN` require `SELECT`/`INDEX`/`ADMIN ON CLUSTER`; M8 `SET CONFIG` requires `ADMIN ON CLUSTER`. Operations mode never adds or bypasses a check
- [x] No raw encryption key exposure — Operations mode has no key access and never imports `internal/crypto`/`storage`/`wal`/`catalog` (enforced by an `imports_test.go` boundary test); `system.tls`/`system.key_versions` structurally cannot carry key material; the M5 backup path runs server-side (nextsqld holds the keys), never in Admin
- [x] Cluster/backup/security status reflects server truth — every view reads live `system.*` (or issues a live statement) through the operator's own connection: server/storage/replication/replica-health, databases/realms, sessions/queries/transactions/locks, users/roles/grants, TLS/key-rotation/audit-chain status, tables/indexes/stats, running config vs on-disk config, process metrics, server-log tail, and the verified backup list — no value is derived from local UI state

# Phase 29 — NextSQL Studio (Studio mode of NextSQL Admin)

NextSQL Studio is the official database development IDE. As of the 2026-09-05 merge
(log #142), it is not a separate product or binary — it is the **Studio mode** of the
unified `nextsql-admin` binary, alongside Setup mode and Operations mode (Phase 28).
`internal/admin/studio` now owns the contracts, bounded result collector, and streaming
framer for M1/M2's authenticated query workspace; `docs/design-admin-studio.md` audits exactly what is
implemented, tested, and still open. This phase's checklist remains the authority for
what Studio mode must become. Its eventual connection model differs from
Operations mode's single-operator session (below, saved multi-environment connection
profiles vs. one implicit session) — that is a real difference in what each mode
connects to, not a reason to split it back into a separate product.

## Studio product goals

Primary users:

```text
developers
DBAs
data engineers
backend engineers
system architects
```

Core rule: **Do not build a generic SQL client with a NextSQL logo.** Studio must understand NextSQL-native SQL, JSON, FTS, vectors, hybrid search, geo, realms/databases, workflows, migrations, and query plans.

## Core architecture

- [x] Studio communicates through official SDK/NSQL — M1 uses only `drivers/go` on the authenticated Admin session
- [x] Capability negotiation with server — M1 bootstraps from live `system.capabilities`
- [x] Studio never reads pages/WAL/catalog files directly — compiler-enforced import audit
- [x] Studio never requires server root unlock key — no key/data-directory surface or import
- [x] Studio never bypasses RBAC or realm/database isolation — catalog and SQL run as the logged-in user; directly verified end to end by `TestAdminStudioEnforcesRBAC` (log #175)
- [ ] Secure OS credential storage where available
- [x] Ask-every-time fallback instead of plaintext secret files — M1 reuses Operations login and persists no credential

## Main shell / UX

- [x] Professional desktop IDE layout — M1 responsive explorer/editor/inspector composition
- [ ] Connection Explorer
- [x] Editor workspace — M1 single-editor surface
- [~] Result/plan/messages/statistics panel — the result area has all four facets: the virtualized grid, the graphical EXPLAIN plan tree, messages (query-error + truncation alerts), and a statistics status line (`queryResultSummary`) that now reports `N rows · M columns · T ms` for a read and `N rows affected` / `Statement completed` for a column-less write/DDL instead of a misleading "0 rows" (log #195). Not restructured into an explicit tab strip.
- [x] Inspector panel — capabilities or lazy selected-table metadata
- [x] Global command palette — Ctrl/Cmd+K (or a **Commands** button) opens a `Modal` combobox (`CommandPalette.tsx`) over ~18 existing Studio actions — run/cancel/new-tab, open each explorer, switch connection, saved queries, schema diagram, GRANT/REVOKE builder. Pure `rankCommandMatches` scoring (exact→prefix→substring→subsequence, hidden per-command keywords, curated order for an empty query, disabled commands filtered out). No route, no server surface (log #194)
- [~] Recent connections/projects home screen — the Switch-connection modal offers the realm/database pairs recently switched to on the current `nextsqld` (per host+user `localStorage`, no credential, bounded at 10) as quick-fill buttons (log #193). A full landing/home screen still needs the multi-target model.
- [x] Light/dark/system themes — inherited from the shared Admin shell and browser-tested
- [x] Layout persistence without credentials — explorer/inspector visibility and pixel widths plus the last selected table name are mirrored to `localStorage` per connection (`nextsql-studio-layout:…`, never a credential/SQL/result); accessible `role="separator"` splitters (24px hit target, arrow/Home/End) resize the panes; Hide/Show + command-palette **Reset layout** restore the defaults; a stored table is re-selected only if it still appears in the authorized bootstrap list (log #203)
- [x] Keyboard-first navigation — shared shell navigation plus Ctrl/Cmd+Enter execution and focusable result scroll regions
- [x] Accessibility baseline — M1 states pass the real-Chrome axe WCAG 2.2 A/AA audit
- [x] High-DPI support — real Chrome at DPR 2 verifies the compact Studio layout, no document-level horizontal overflow, no undersized raster sources, loaded bundled scalable fonts, and axe WCAG 2.2 AA; the same regression helper covers Setup and Operations before restoring default device metrics (log #202)
- [x] Crash recovery for unsaved editors — each editor tab's title + SQL text (not results/errors/plan/history) is mirrored to `localStorage` (debounced 500 ms, per-connection key, every access try/caught) and rehydrated on load via pure bounded `serializeEditorDrafts`/`parseEditorDrafts` (≤8 tabs, ≤200k chars/buffer, malformed → no draft). A `role="status"` notice offers **Start fresh**; `editorDraftsWorthRestoring` suppresses it for the pristine default buffer. Deliberate narrow exception to the "query history never persists" rule — documented (log #183)

## Connection manager

- [~] Name/host/port/database/user — the session's realm and database are switchable in place (`Switch connection…`, log #191); host/port stays the one `nextsql-admin` process target until multi-host named profiles land
- [ ] TLS/CA/client-certificate fields as supported
- [~] Realm/database profile — switchable per session via `POST /api/v1/studio/reconnect`; not yet a saved named profile (log #191)
- [~] Read-consistency profile — the session's read-consistency mode (strong / bounded + staleness / stale) is settable live via `POST /api/v1/studio/read-consistency` (a driver session-control frame, no reconnect; reads only; `409` if a query is in flight; toolbar `Select` + a "stale reads" warning badge). Not yet a saved named profile (log #192)
- [ ] Secure saved password option
- [~] Dev/test/staging/production environment profiles — the **current** connection can be tagged (dev/test/staging/production) via a per-viewer browser preference keyed by realm/database/user; a full multi-profile switcher still needs the multi-target connection model (log #176)
- [x] Highly visible production indicator — a standing `role="alert"` banner while the connection is tagged production (log #176)
- [x] Production safety mode — read-only mode: `POST /api/v1/studio/query/analyze` now returns a `write` flag (mirrors nextsqld's `executor.isMutating` at the AST level); while read-only mode is on, a write statement (single or in a script) asks for confirmation before running, individually overridable (log #176)
- [x] Warn UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE using parsed AST — `POST /api/v1/studio/query/analyze` parses with `internal/sql/parser` (log #150)
- [x] Warn destructive DDL — same endpoint flags `DROP TABLE`/`INDEX`/`USER`/`ROLE`/`WORKFLOW`/`TRIGGER`/`SCHEDULE`/`RESOURCE GROUP` and `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN`/`DROP PARTITION` (log #150)
- [x] Optional read-only production session default — read-only mode turns **on** automatically for a production-tagged connection (the user can toggle it off for the session) (log #176)

## Database explorer / schema tooling

- [x] Lazy-loaded database/schema/table/index/workflow tree — the Database explorer is now a two-branch disclosure tree (`SchemaTree.tsx`): **Tables** (from the bootstrap list; expanding a table node fetches its `GET /api/v1/studio/table` bundle once and shows lazy Columns / Indexes / Foreign keys sub-branches; selecting a name still loads the full inspector) and a read-only **Workflows** branch (lazily runs the existing `GET /api/v1/studio/workflows` on first open). No new route/server surface; RBAC stays the sole authority (log #177, FK sub-branch added #179)
- [x] Table overview — lazy authorized `system.tables` detail
- [x] Columns — lazy authorized `system.columns` detail
- [x] Primary/foreign keys — PK columns tagged `PK` in the Columns view/tree from `system.columns.is_primary`; a **Foreign keys** inspector section (outbound constraints + an inbound **Referenced by** grid) + a schema-tree sub-branch render the table's FKs from `system.foreign_keys` added to the `GET /api/v1/studio/table` bundle (not `required`), table-visibility-filtered like `system.columns` (logs #178–#180); a whole-schema ER diagram is the "Schema diagram…" explorer (log #181)
- [x] Constraints — a bounded unified inspector grid composes PK + NOT NULL (`system.columns`), UNIQUE indexes (`system.indexes`, kept honestly labelled as indexes with predicate/include/status), and grouped FKs (`system.foreign_keys`) from the existing authorized table-detail bundle; composite key order follows catalog ordinals, an older-server `PRIMARY` backing-index row is not duplicated, and NextSQL's lack of `CHECK` is not hidden (log #189)
- [x] Indexes — lazy authorized `system.indexes` detail
- [x] Statistics — lazy authorized `system.table_stats` (row count, updated_at) + `system.index_stats` (per-index row count) in a bounded "Statistics" inspector section; ANALYZE-written estimates, explicitly labelled as such, with a "run ANALYZE" note when unpopulated (log #171)
- [x] DDL view — the table inspector's **DDL** section shows the canonical `CREATE TABLE` + `CREATE INDEX` script for the selected table, from `system.table_ddl` rows added to the `GET /api/v1/studio/table` bundle (not `required` — a server without the view degrades to no panel). Focusable `<pre>` + **Copy DDL** + **Open in editor**. `system.table_ddl` itself: `table_name, object_type, object_name, ddl`; shared `internal/catalog/ddl` renderer; table-visibility-filtered like `system.columns` (server view log #187, Studio panel log #188)
- [~] Dependencies — the table inspector's **Dependencies** section composes the inbound **Referenced by** FK grid (`system.foreign_keys WHERE ref_table = …`, log #180) with a **Triggers** grid of the row triggers defined on the table (`system.triggers WHERE table_name = …`, added to the `GET /api/v1/studio/table` bundle, not `required`; matching per-table schema-tree sub-branch), log #199. What remains needs catalog surfaces that don't exist: workflow/trigger *body* source text that free-references a table (NextSQL has no views)
- [x] Table designer — a **Design schema…** modal (`SchemaDesignerExplorer.tsx`) in Table mode builds a native `CREATE TABLE` from named columns (closed NextSQL type list with CHAR/VARCHAR/DECIMAL/VECTOR parameters), PRIMARY KEY (required; inline when single, table-level when composite), optional one FOREIGN KEY, and DEFAULT UUID()/NOW()/AI()/literal; live preview as you edit; Insert loads the SQL into the editor for review — never executes, no new route (log #205)
- [x] Index designer — the same modal in Index mode builds `CREATE INDEX` / `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` / `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` / `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` / `CREATE SPATIAL INDEX` from authorized `system.columns` of a chosen table (kind list restricted to what those columns can actually support; JSON path, INCLUDE, analyzer, USING method/quantization/IVF options); live preview; never executes (log #205)
- [x] Generated native DDL preview — the inspector read path (log #188) plus live preview-as-you-edit in the table/index designer (log #205); the emitted text is the same quoted native DDL the operator will run
- [x] ER diagram from actual FKs — a "Schema diagram…" modal explorer over `GET /api/v1/studio/schema-graph` (whole-catalog `system.foreign_keys`, 4,000-row cap, RBAC-filtered): pure `buildSchemaGraph`/`layoutSchemaGraph` place tables in dependency layers (cycles broken), rendered as an inline `<svg role="img">` with a grouped **Relationships** list as its text alternative + large-schema fallback (>40 tables / >80 FKs → list only). No layout library added (log #181)
- [x] Global object search — a "Search objects…" modal finder (`ObjectSearch.tsx`) over the two namespaces Studio enumerates completely without a per-object fetch: table names (bootstrap) + workflow names (one `system.workflows` read, loaded on first open). Pure `rankObjectMatches` ranks exact → prefix → substring → in-order subsequence, never a non-subsequence guess; keyboard-driven (`role=combobox`/`listbox`, arrows + Enter). Selecting a table opens it in the inspector, a workflow opens the Workflows explorer. Columns/indexes are not searched (would need a fetch per table) — noted in the UI (log #182)

## SQL editor

- [ ] NextSQL-native syntax highlighting
- [x] Line numbers/bracket matching/indentation — shared RUI editor behavior
- [x] Multi-tab editing — independent SQL buffer/result/error per tab, bounded at 8; the server's one-active-query-per-session limit is surfaced as a disabled "Busy…" Run action plus a cross-tab notice rather than ever attempting a second concurrent query (log #154)
- [x] Execute statement — one bounded request via the authenticated official-driver connection
- [x] Execute selection — a non-empty editor text selection runs (and is analyzed for the confirm-before-run check) as its own statement instead of the whole buffer (log #151)
- [x] Execute script — `POST /api/v1/studio/query/split` tokenizes the buffer with a real lexer pass (`internal/admin/studio.SplitScript`); the browser analyzes every statement and shows one consolidated destructive-statement warning, then runs them sequentially through the bounded non-streaming query path, stopping at the first failure/cancellation (log #155)
- [x] Cancel query — session-scoped query id; live lock-wait cancellation and connection reuse tested
- [x] Prepared parameters — a buffer referencing positional `$1..$N` shows a per-tab **Parameters** panel (one text input + a NULL checkbox per distinct placeholder; ephemeral, never persisted). Run sends a dense positional `params` array on `POST /api/v1/studio/query{,/stream}`; `studio.ValidateParams` bounds it (≤32 params, ≤64 KiB/value, 413 past either) and `studio.ParamValues` binds each as a string (server coerces to the expected type) or a typed SQL NULL. Single-statement Run only — not explorers or Execute Script (log #186)
- [x] SQL formatting — a **Format** editor button (Shift+Alt+F) + command-palette entry reflows the active tab's SQL through pure `formatSQL` (`resultTools.ts`): a self-contained, **comment-preserving** tokenizer (deliberately not `internal/sql/lexer`, which drops comments and folds case) + a clause-level reflow — normalize whitespace, uppercase only lexer keywords, break a line before each top-level clause keyword / JOIN / `AND`/`OR` (with `BETWEEN…AND` and `CASE…END` guards), one-per-line SELECT/SET/VALUES lists. Strict safety net: the output is re-tokenized and must yield the identical significant-token stream (keywords case-insensitive, everything else byte-for-byte, comments in order) or the buffer is returned **unchanged** — as it also is on any unterminated string/comment/quoted-identifier or an over-1-MiB buffer. Never executes, no route. Parenthesized groups (column-def lists, VALUES tuples, subqueries) stay on one line by design. Unit-tested in `test-studio-results.mjs` (log #218)
- [x] Find/replace — literal substring search over the active tab's own buffer, wrap-around navigate/replace/replace-all, no highlight overlay needed since it moves the real textarea selection (log #157)
- [x] Context-aware IntelliSense from live catalog — bounded table/column-name suggestion list, catalog identifiers only (no keyword completion, see log #169's honesty note); tables free from bootstrap, columns lazily fetched per FROM/JOIN-referenced table only while the panel is open, capped 16-table cache (log #169)
- [x] JSON-path completion where metadata is known — with the caret inside a dotted path, IntelliSense switches to the native JSON paths a FROM/JOIN-referenced table is actually **indexed** on (from its authorized `system.indexes` rows — the only JSON structure NextSQL exposes metadata for); never a guessed path (log #174)
- [x] Vector-aware completion — when the caret is in a `NEAREST` column slot or a `USING` metric slot of the current statement, IntelliSense switches to VECTOR/BITVECTOR/SPARSEVECTOR columns (and that column kind's exact SQL metrics: `COSINE`/`L2`/`INNER_PRODUCT`/`HAMMING`) from the same authorized `api.studioTable()` fetch already used for table/column/JSON-path completion; `TO (...)` is not a completion slot (no per-element catalog); `CREATE INDEX … USING` is ignored (log #204)
- [~] Inline parser/binder diagnostics — **parser** half done (log #220): `parser.ParseDiag` attaches the stopped-on token's byte offset at the top of `Parse` (no change to the ~100 individual error sites); `studio.Diagnostics` splits the buffer with the `SplitScript` lexer pass, `ParseDiag`s each statement, and maps offsets back to whole-buffer UTF-16 line/column; `POST /api/v1/studio/query/diagnostics` (parser-only, no connection/query slot); the editor shows a debounced strip with a **Go to error** control (RUI `CodeEditor` still has no overlay primitive). **Binder** half stays open — the binder discards both the identifier and its position, and `nextsql-admin` has no catalog to resolve names against; needs the binder to carry positions + nextsqld to return them in the NSQL error frame, or Admin-side catalog introspection
- [x] Deterministic suggestions for misspelled identifiers where safe — bare FROM/JOIN table names only, the one place NextSQL's grammar makes an identifier's role unambiguous; column/alias/function-name suggestions are deliberately excluded (no safe way to tell them apart from a regex alone) (log #170)
- [x] Query history with privacy controls — bounded in-memory per-session list (never persisted to storage or sent anywhere), most-recent-first, records outcome/rows/elapsed, click to reload without re-executing, explicit Clear (log #152)
- [x] Saved queries/folders/tags — a "Saved" popover (`SavedQueries.tsx`) keeps named, comma-tag-grouped SQL snippets mirrored to `localStorage` per connection (text only, never sent anywhere). A folder is a tag: the panel filters by a tag `Select` + free text over name/SQL. Each entry loads into the active tab (no auto-run), can be **Update**d with the current buffer, renamed inline, or deleted. Pure bounded codec (`serializeSavedQueries`/`parseSavedQueries`/`upsertSavedQuery`/`removeSavedQuery`/`filterSavedQueries`/`savedQueryTags` — ≤200 entries, ≤200k chars SQL, ≤10 tags, malformed→empty), unit-tested (log #184)
- [x] Git-friendly workspace artifacts — the "Saved" popover's **Export…** downloads the set through `exportSavedQueries` (`{format:"nextsql-studio-saved-queries-v1",queries}`, ordered by name→id, 2-space indent, trailing newline → byte-identical regardless of save order); **Import…** reads a file (`parseSavedQueriesExport`, ≤48 MiB, wrapper or bare array) and `mergeSavedQueries` merges by id (add / replace-if-newer-and-changed / leave-older-alone, recency-ordered, cap 200), reporting added/updated/unchanged in a `role="status"` notice. Pure helpers, unit-tested (log #185)

## Results / data editing

- [x] Streaming virtualized result grid — M2 `/api/v1/studio/query/stream` emits ordered NDJSON metadata + ≤128-row/256-KiB-target batches + one completion frame; the browser incrementally consumes them and mounts only the visible fixed-height row window plus bounded overscan (log #147)
- [x] No full materialization of huge results — Admin no longer materializes the browser query path; M2 streams up to 5,000 rows/8 MiB/25 seconds with a 1 MiB raw-row ceiling, while the browser independently enforces the same finite bounds and virtualizes the DOM (log #147)
- [x] Cell/row/selection copy — active-cell raw copy plus selected/all loaded rows as bounded, spreadsheet-formula-neutralized TSV; one selected row is the row-copy path (M3, log #148)
- [x] Export selected/streamed data — selected rows or the entire currently loaded bounded stream preview export locally as safe CSV or lossless `nextsql-studio-result-v1` JSON; no server result is cached or persisted (M3, log #148)
- [x] JSON tree/raw viewer — bounded 1,024-node/24-level tree plus unchanged raw JSON in the native cell inspector (M3, log #148)
- [x] Vector compact cell representation + inspector — dense/bit/sparse dimension and non-zero summaries, finite/order/dimension validation, L2 norm, and a 256-value rendered window under a 65,536-value parse ceiling (M3, log #148)
- [x] Geo value preview — M3 renders bounded normalized coordinate previews for fixed `POINT`/`BOX`/`LINESTRING`/`POLYGON` values with explicit longitude,latitude order (log #148); extended to general `GEOMETRY`/`GEOGRAPHY` `MULTIPOINT`/`MULTILINESTRING`/`MULTIPOLYGON`/`GEOMETRYCOLLECTION` values, recursively flattened for rendering and never range-checked against WGS84 degrees (log #149)
- [x] Timezone-aware TIMESTAMPTZ display — inspector preserves the canonical server value and shows UTC, browser-local timezone text, and Unix epoch milliseconds; offset-free input fails closed (M3, log #148)
- [x] Editable data grid — detects single-table SELECT over catalog tables (`detectEditableTable`); validates required primary key columns (`isResultEditable`); cell editing via modal (`EditCellModal`, double-click or Edit cell button); row deletion staging (`stageRowDelete`, toggled via Delete row); row insertion staging (`stageRowInsert` via `AddRowModal`); visual highlights for modified cells (`nss-cell-modified`), deleted rows (`nss-row-deleted`), and inserted rows (`nss-row-inserted`) (log #221)
- [x] Parameterized INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE generation — a **Parameterized DML…** toolbar button + command-palette entry opens a modal (`DMLBuilderExplorer.tsx`) that builds a positional-parameter (`$1..$N`) `INSERT` / `UPDATE` / `DELETE` statement *template* for the chosen table from the authorized `system.columns` in the existing `GET /api/v1/studio/table` bundle, loaded into the active editor tab for review — never executed, no new route. Pure `buildParameterizedDML`/`dmlDefaultColumns` (`resultTools.ts`): `INSERT` = one placeholder per chosen column (default all, catalog order); `UPDATE` = `SET` list (default non-PK) then `WHERE` key list (default PK), params numbered SET-then-WHERE, SET/WHERE overlap rejected; `DELETE` = `WHERE` key list (default PK); `UPDATE`/`DELETE` require ≥1 WHERE key; `quoteIdentifier` on every name; placeholder count capped at `MAX_QUERY_PARAMS` (32, the editor's Parameters-panel / `studio.MaxQueryParams` bound). The emitted `$1..$N` are bound by the existing positional Parameters panel (log #186). The Studio query-tab strip switched from multi-row wrap to a single horizontally scrolling row (log #201)
- [x] Staged-change review — review modal (`StagedChangesReviewModal`) displays staged updates, deletions, and insertions with per-item removal, discard-all, and transactional SQL preview with copy and open-in-editor actions (log #221)
- [x] Transactional commit/discard where appropriate — generates atomic `BEGIN; ... COMMIT;` transaction script (`buildStagedChangeSQL`); commits sequentially over the authenticated session connection with fail-safe rollback on error; re-executes query to refresh grid; Discard all resets staged state (log #221)

## EXPLAIN / profiler

- [x] Graphical `EXPLAIN` tree — client-side parse of the existing `EXPLAIN`/`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` result columns into a nested tree, no server change (log #153)
- [x] Graphical `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` — same tree renders measured rows/time/cpu/memory/disk/cache/spill/workers/index when the statement was ANALYZE (log #153)
- [x] Estimated vs actual rows — every node shows its estimated rows; ANALYZE results additionally show actual rows (log #153)
- [x] CPU/memory/disk/cache/spill/workers/index display — shown per node, only when ANALYZE actually measured them (log #153)
- [x] Highlight estimation errors — `explainEstimateSeverity` flags a >=10x (error) or >=3x (warning) miss between estimated and actual rows (log #153)
- [x] Plan comparison — one deep-copied, tab-local baseline capped at 512 operators; deterministic structural-path alignment labels added/removed/operator/metric changes and never guesses semantic node identity (log #167)
- [x] Query profiler breakdown — ANALYZE-only, capped at 512 operators; structural per-operator table, estimate-error signals, and reported maxima with inclusive/query-level metric caveats; never sums operators or invents percentages (log #168)
- [x] Never display guessed metrics as measured — measured fields (actual rows/time/cpu/memory/disk/cache/spill/workers) render only when the statement was `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`; a plain `EXPLAIN` shows an explicit "Estimates only" notice and nothing else (log #153)

## Native NextSQL explorers

### JSON Explorer

- [x] Tree/raw/path browser — the bounded JSON result-cell tree/raw inspector now makes every object/array/scalar node selectable and shows its exact NextSQL-native path (log #159)
- [x] Copy JSON path — the selected safely quoted native path is copyable without executing anything (log #159)
- [x] Indexed-path indicator — compares only against the selected table's authorized `system.indexes`; names valid matches, surfaces non-valid status, and reports ambiguous rather than guessing for special keys whose segment boundaries the current dotted catalog text cannot prove (log #159)
- [x] Generate native JSON-path query — inserts `SELECT <path> FROM <table> LIMIT 100` into the active editor; the exact quoted identifier + numeric array-index shape is parser-pinned and never auto-executes (log #159)

### Full-text Explorer

- [x] Select table/column/index — capability-gated authorized table metadata; valid index selection locks exact catalog field order, while automatic mode permits the shipped sequential fallback; ambiguous/non-valid metadata fails closed (log #160)
- [x] Search phrase — bounded 4,096-character native phrase input preserves phrase quotes, prefix `*`, fuzzy `~`, and typo-tolerance syntax for server validation (log #160)
- [x] BM25 rank display — result grid adds a UI-only ordinal rank from the server's score-descending row order and explicitly says numeric scores are not exposed (log #160)
- [x] Matched terms/highlight when supported — rows/HIGHLIGHT/SNIPPET modes generate native select-list calls; markers stay visible literal text and are never interpreted as HTML (log #160)
- [x] Generate/copy SQL — identifiers/literals are safely quoted; Copy and Insert never execute, while explicit Run search uses the existing bounded authenticated Studio stream (log #160)

### Vector Explorer

- [x] Select table/vector column — capability-gated authorized `system.columns` metadata; lists VECTOR/BITVECTOR/SPARSEVECTOR columns, defaulting to the first; a matching `system.indexes` vector index is surfaced with its status (single-column-only, so an empty/comma-containing catalog field is unconditionally unusable rather than guessed) (log #161)
- [x] Paste/enter vector — accepts `[…]`, `(…)`, or a bare comma list and normalizes to the exact native parenthesized `NEAREST … TO (…)` literal grammar (log #161)
- [x] Metric selection — options are exactly the column-kind-appropriate subset (`COSINE`/`L2`/`INNER_PRODUCT` for dense, `HAMMING` only for `BITVECTOR`, `COSINE`/`INNER_PRODUCT` for `SPARSEVECTOR`), verified to match server-side rejection exactly against a real running `nextsqld` (log #161)
- [x] Top-K — bounded 1–100 `LIMIT` (log #161)
- [x] HNSW search settings when supported — checked, not assumed: `internal/sql/parser`'s `nearestClause` parses only `col TO <expr> [USING metric]`, so there is no per-query HNSW/IVF/IVFPQ search-time tuning knob anywhere in NSQL (`WITH (QUANTIZATION=…)`/`WITH (LISTS=…, PROBES=…)` are `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` build-time options only); the explorer states this instead of rendering inert controls (log #161)
- [x] Vector inspector — a live panel parses the pasted literal and shows value count, L2 norm, and non-zero count as it's typed (log #161)
- [x] Validate dimensions — the same live inspector fails closed when the parsed value count doesn't match the column's declared `<...,N>`, and rejects non-0/1 values for a `BITVECTOR` column (log #161)

### Hybrid Explorer

- [x] Structured filter builder — a single optional `column operator value` condition; only columns that coerce cleanly from a bare literal (exact/unsigned integers, DECIMAL, STRING/TEXT/UUID/TIMESTAMPTZ) are offered, and only `=`/`<>`/`<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=`/`IS NULL`/`IS NOT NULL` — NextSQL has no LIKE/regex operator (log #162)
- [x] Full-text input — same catalog-driven column/index/phrase builder as the standalone Full-text Explorer (log #162)
- [x] Vector input — same catalog-driven column/metric/vector builder as the standalone Vector Explorer (log #162)
- [x] Metric/limit — vector metric restricted to the column-kind-valid set; a single shared 1–100 result limit (log #162)
- [x] Generated SQL — exact native `[WHERE ...] SEARCH ... FOR '...' NEAREST ... USING metric LIMIT n` hybrid grammar, verified clause order against a real running `nextsqld` (log #162)
- [x] Execution plan — an "Explain" action runs `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of the exact generated SQL through the existing bounded stream; the already-implemented graphical EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE tree (log #153) renders it automatically with no new rendering code (log #162)
- [x] Candidate counts where available — satisfied by the same generic tree: each `Candidates` node's own estimated/actual rows figure is the candidate count, confirmed against a real hybrid `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` plan (log #162)
- [x] BM25/vector/hybrid rank inspector where engine exposes it — results show a truthful ordinal "Hybrid rank" (not "BM25 rank") from server row order, stating that NextSQL's reciprocal-rank-fusion score itself is not exposed by the current result schema (log #162)

### Geo Explorer

- [x] POINT/LINESTRING/POLYGON rendering — reuses the existing `CellInspector` `GeoView` SVG renderer unchanged for a zoomed confirmation preview of the drawn point/polygon (log #163)
- [x] Draw point/radius/polygon — a fixed equirectangular world-extent SVG canvas (click-to-place, `aria-hidden`) plus keyboard-accessible Longitude/Latitude/Radius number fields and Add/Remove-vertex controls as the actual accessible path (log #163)
- [x] Generate native geo SQL — `WHERE DWITHIN(col, POINT(lon, lat), meters)` or `WHERE WITHIN(col, POLYGON('(...)'))` over an auto-closed ring; literal shapes checked directly against `internal/sql/types/geo.go`'s `EvalGeo`/`ParseWKT` (log #163)
- [x] Preserve longitude,latitude order — every field, generated literal, and preview is longitude-then-latitude throughout, matching `docs/geo.md` (log #163)

## Developer operations

- [x] Transaction console — read-only live transaction/session/query snapshot reusing Operations mode's authorized `api.activity()` read, refreshed on every open and explicit Refresh; no fabricated cross-session rollback/kill action (log #165)
- [x] Lock explorer — read-only live `system.locks` snapshot in the same bounded panel, with table/mode/granted state and the same server-side visibility; no new Admin route (log #165)
- [x] Realm/database selector / reconnect — a **Switch connection…** toolbar control (`SwitchConnection.tsx`) re-targets the session's NSQL connection to a different realm/database on the same `nextsqld` via `POST /api/v1/studio/reconnect` (a fresh authenticated connection swapped in atomically by `session.reconnect`; `409` if a query is in flight; a failed open leaves the old connection intact). Password supplied each time, never stored. The new realm/database flow through `who` and remount the workspace on the new connection; per-connection localStorage scopes re-key. Multi-**host** named profiles remain open (log #191)
- [x] Visible cross-database administration warning — parsed-AST `realm_scoped` classification for `CREATE`/`DROP USER` and `CREATE`/`DROP ROLE`; single-query and consolidated-script confirmations name the connected realm and database, retaining both realm and destructive reasons when both apply (log #197)
- [x] Users/roles privilege explorer — read-only `system.users`/`system.roles`/`system.grants` view reusing Operations mode's admin-only `api.security()` read (no new server route); each grant row's "Revoke…" action reverses it into a prefilled GRANT/REVOKE builder rather than executing anything itself (log #164)
- [x] GRANT/REVOKE builder — client-side generator, no new server route; inserts into the editor for review/RBAC like any hand-typed statement (log #156)
- [x] Audit viewer — read-only `system.audit_verify` chain status + bounded 200-row `system.audit_log` tail reusing Operations mode's admin-only `api.security()` read and exact status renderer; live open/Refresh, no polling or mutation controls (log #166)
- [~] Migration workspace using official migration system — the **read side** is implemented: a **Migrations…** explorer (`GET /api/v1/studio/migrations`) shows the database's `nsql_schema_migrations` history (version/name/applied_at/execution_ms/dirty/direction) through the logged-in operator's own connection, with a current-version/dirty-state summary and a `role="alert"` for any dirty version (log #196). Authoring/validating/dry-running/applying/reverting stays with the `nextsql migrate` CLI — they need the local migration files a protocol-only Admin client never holds
- [~] Create/validate/dry-run/pending/apply/down/status/repair — **status** (applied history + current version + dirty detection) is read-only in the Migrations explorer (log #196); the mutating verbs remain file-bound to the CLI
- [ ] Schema diff (later)
- [~] CSV/JSON/NDJSON import/export — **import** is an **Import data…** modal (`ImportExplorer.tsx`) that parses a pasted/loaded CSV/semicolon/TSV/JSON-array/NDJSON document, auto-maps its fields to the target table's authorized `system.columns` (per-field overrides), and builds a bounded, type-checked `INSERT` script (`parseImportText`/`buildImportInsertSQL`, `resultTools.ts`: ≤8 MiB in, ≤2,000 rows, 100-row batches, ≤1 MiB SQL, quoted identifiers/strings, int/bool/JSON cells validated with named row errors, empty→NULL toggle + NOT-NULL block) into the editor for review — never executes, no new route (reuses `GET /api/v1/studio/table`). Result **export** (selected/streamed rows → safe CSV / lossless JSON) is already done (see "Results / data editing"). Log #200
- [ ] Streaming bulk import
- [x] Data generator for development — a **Generate data…** toolbar button + command-palette entry opens a modal (`DataGeneratorExplorer.tsx`) that builds `INSERT` statements of synthetic rows from the authorized `system.columns` metadata already in the `GET /api/v1/studio/table` bundle and loads them into the active editor tab for review — no new route, never executes. Pure bounded `dataGenColumns`/`buildDataGeneratorSQL` (`resultTools.ts`): ≤1,000 rows, 100-row `INSERT` batches, ≤512 KiB, `quoteIdentifier`/`quoteSQLString` on every name/value, deterministic per seed (mulberry32). Per-column strategies for `INT8..64`/`UINT8..64`/`DECIMAL`/`STRING`/`TEXT`/`UUID`/`BOOL`/`TIMESTAMPTZ`/`JSON`; every other declared type is badged "not generatable" and omitted; a NOT-NULL-no-default column that would be omitted is a blocking error (log #198)
- [x] Vector dataset import — an **Import vector dataset…** toolbar/command-palette modal (`VectorImportExplorer.tsx`) that maps one embedding field of a pasted/loaded CSV/JSON/NDJSON document onto a table's `VECTOR`/`BITVECTOR`/`SPARSEVECTOR` column (any other fields onto scalar columns) and builds a bounded `INSERT` script into the editor for review — never executes, no new route (reuses `GET /api/v1/studio/table`). Pure `buildVectorImportSQL`/`autoVectorImportField` (`resultTools.ts`): each embedding cell validated against the column's declared dimensions + `BITVECTOR` 0/1 domain via the Vector Explorer's `parseVectorLiteralInput`, emitted as the native parenthesized literal (`VALUES ((1, 0, …))`), catalog-ordinal column order, `quoteIdentifier` on every name, scalar cells reuse the CSV/JSON importer's per-kind checks + 100-row batching; bounds ≤8 MiB in / ≤1 MiB SQL / ≤1,000 rows / ≤262,144 rows×dims with an actionable ceiling error (log #219)
- [ ] nextsql-bench result viewer and run comparison
- [x] Heavy/destructive benchmarks blocked on production by default — `cmd/nextsql-bench` detects production profile (`--production`, `NEXTSQL_PROFILE=production`, or `nextsql.conf` `deployment_profile=production`) and blocks heavy or mutating benchmarks (destructive bulk UPDATE/DELETE in SLO suite, large row/vector scale, cluster read-scaling, and mutating SQL workloads) via `bench.CheckProductionWorkload` unless `--allow-production-benchmark` is explicitly passed (log #246)

Applies to Setup, Operations, and Studio.
