    **Wire byte layouts** (from `internal/sql/types/row.go`'s `encodeScalar`, the wire-scalar path — distinct from `encodeSortable`, the index-key path, which sign-bit-flips `DATE` but the wire scalar does not): `CHAR`/`VARCHAR` — `u32` LE length prefix + UTF-8 bytes (identical to `STRING`/`TEXT`). `DATE` — 4-byte LE signed `int32` day count, no sign flip. `TIME` — 8-byte LE nanoseconds-since-midnight, always non-negative. `TIMESTAMP` (naive) — 8-byte LE signed nanoseconds-since-epoch, byte-identical to `TIMESTAMPTZ`, semantics-only difference (no offset applied). `FLOAT32`/`FLOAT64` — plain 4/8-byte LE IEEE-754.

    **JS-family** (`drivers/js/protocol.mjs`, shared by Bun/Deno; `drivers/node/nextsql.js`, independent implementation): `Kind.Date=23`/`Time=24`/`Char=25`/`Varchar=26`/`Timestamp=27`/`Float32=28`/`Float64=29` added to both. `encodeDate`/`encodeTime`/`encodeNaiveTimestamp`/`encodeFloat32`/`encodeFloat64` helpers wired into `encodeParam` via `{kind:'date'|'time'|'timestamp'|'float32'|'float64', value}` wrappers — `date`/`timestamp` accept a `Date` (a bare `Date` still defaults to `TimestampTZ`, unchanged); `time` accepts nanoseconds-since-midnight as a plain number (fits safely in a JS double, max ~8.64e13 well under 2^53, so no BigInt needed unlike `TIME`'s own field). `decodeValue` gained `Kind.Char`/`Varchar` sharing `String`/`Text`'s case, and new `Date`/`Time`/`Timestamp`/`Float32`/`Float64` cases. `drivers/js/types.d.ts` updated. Tests: `drivers/node/nextsql.test.js` (`DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP/CHAR/VARCHAR/FLOAT32/FLOAT64 param round-trip`, incl. pre-1970 `DATE`, NaN/Infinity `FLOAT32`/`FLOAT64` distinguishing `0`/`-0` via sign, a hand-built `CHAR` wire fixture) — 23/23. `drivers/bun/nextsql.test.js`/`drivers/deno/nextsql_test.js` (`DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP/FLOAT32/FLOAT64 param round-trip`) — 21/21 each.

    **PHP** (`drivers/php/src/{Client,Protocol}.php`): `KIND_DATE`..`KIND_FLOAT64` added. `encodeParam` gained `date`/`time`/`timestamp`/`float32`/`float64` array-wrapper cases; `decodeValue` gained matching cases; `decodeRowDesc`'s existing generic 6-byte-header path needed no change (only `ENUM`'s variable-length labels ever required that). **Two real, pre-existing bugs found and fixed, both predating this session and affecting `TIMESTAMPTZ` too, not just the new `TIMESTAMP` type** (found by testing the new `TIMESTAMP`/`DATE` encode paths against pre-1970 values, since they share the exact same helper functions `TIMESTAMPTZ`'s own encode/decode already used):
    1. **Encode**: `$v instanceof \DateTimeInterface` (the existing `TIMESTAMPTZ` path) computed `$ns` as a string and passed it to `u64fromDec()`, which calls `decToBytes()` — a pure-unsigned decimal-digit-string-to-bytes converter that does `(int) $digits[$i]` per character with no sign handling. For a negative `$ns` (any pre-1970 instant), the leading `'-'` character silently becomes digit `0` (PHP's `(int)` cast on a non-digit string returns `0`), producing completely wrong bytes with no error. Reproduced directly: `u64fromDec("-86400000000000")` → `00004f91944e0000` versus the correct `0000b16e6bb1ffff` (verified against `pack('q', -86400000000000)`).
    2. **Decode**: the existing `KIND_TIMESTAMPTZ` case computed `$sec = intdiv($ns, 1_000_000_000)` and `$usec = intdiv($ns % 1_000_000_000, 1000)`. PHP's `%` returns a result with the *dividend's* sign (unlike Python/Ruby's floor-based `%`), so for negative `$ns` this produces a negative `$usec`; `sprintf('%d.%06d', $sec, $usec)` then emits something like `"-86400.-500000"`, and `DateTimeImmutable::createFromFormat('U.u', ...)` silently returns `false` instead of raising — a decode that looks like it succeeded (no exception) but hands the caller `false` where a `DateTimeImmutable` was expected. Reproduced directly with `$ns = -86400500000000`.

    **Fix**: added `Protocol::i64le(int $n): string` (`pack('P', $n)` — packs a native PHP int's own two's-complement bit pattern directly, correct for the full signed range, since PHP int already *is* a signed 64-bit register) replacing `u64fromDec()` at all three i64-range call sites (`TIMESTAMPTZ` encode, and the two new `TIMESTAMP`/`TIME` encode paths — `TIME` isn't actually negative in practice, but switched for consistency and to avoid the decimal-string round-trip entirely). `u64fromDec()`/`decToBytes()` themselves are untouched and remain correct — they're still needed for `UINT64`, whose magnitude can exceed `PHP_INT_MAX` and genuinely requires unsigned big-number string arithmetic; the bug was specifically about reusing that unsigned-only helper for a signed i64-range value. Added `Protocol::splitNanos(int $ns): array` (floor-based sec/usec split, `$usec` always in `[0, 999999]`) replacing the inline `intdiv`/`%` pair at both the `TIMESTAMPTZ` and new `TIMESTAMP` decode cases. Also fixed the **`DATE` encode path itself** (new code, not a pre-existing bug, but the same bug class) to floor-divide epoch-seconds by 86400 for the day count rather than using `intdiv()`'s truncate-toward-zero, which would have put a sub-day-boundary pre-1970 instant one day too late.

    **Python** (`drivers/python/nextsql/protocol.py`): `KIND_DATE`..`KIND_FLOAT64` added. Used Python's own distinct, unambiguous native types where possible rather than wrappers: bare `datetime.date` → `DATE` (checked *after* the existing `datetime.datetime` case, since `datetime.datetime` is a `date` subclass — order-dependent and confirmed correct), bare `datetime.time` → `TIME`. **`NaiveTimestamp(value: datetime.datetime)`** wrapper dataclass for `TIMESTAMP`, required because a bare *naive* `datetime.datetime` (`tzinfo is None`) already had an established meaning in this driver before today — "assume UTC, encode as `TimestampTZ`" — and repurposing that existing default to mean the new naive `TIMESTAMP` type instead would have silently changed behavior for any existing caller; deliberately left that default alone and required an explicit wrapper for the new type instead. **`Float32(value)`/`Float64(value)`** dataclasses, since a bare `float` still means `DECIMAL` (requires finite) — needed both to pin the wire width and to send NaN/±Infinity, which `DECIMAL` rejects but the server's `FLOAT32`/`FLOAT64` explicitly support. `Column.labels` used no change (already `None`-defaulted from D11). `decode_row_desc` needed no change (same reasoning as PHP). Note: Python's own `divmod`/`%` are already floor-based (unlike PHP's), so the existing `TIMESTAMPTZ` decode path had no equivalent bug — confirmed by inspection, not just assumed. `TIME` decodes to `datetime.time` at microsecond precision (Python's ceiling; sub-microsecond nanoseconds truncate, the same precision ceiling every timestamp-family value already has in this driver). Exported `EnumValue`... already exported from log #98; newly exported `Float32`, `Float64`, `NaiveTimestamp` from `drivers/python/nextsql/__init__.py`. Tests: `drivers/python/tests/test_protocol.py` — `test_date_round_trip` (incl. pre-1970 and the `datetime`-vs-`date` disambiguation), `test_time_round_trip`, `test_naive_timestamp_round_trip` (incl. confirming a bare naive datetime still defaults to `TimestampTZ`), `test_float_round_trip` (incl. NaN/Infinity, and confirming a bare float still requires finite) — 41/41.

    **Ruby** (`drivers/ruby/lib/nextsql/protocol.rb`, `drivers/ruby/lib/nextsql.rb`): `KIND_DATE`..`KIND_FLOAT64` added. Ruby's `Date` class used directly for bare `DATE` params (checked after the existing `Time, DateTime` case — `DateTime` is `Date`'s own subclass in Ruby's stdlib, confirmed via docs, not assumed — so a bare `Date` correctly falls through only when it isn't also a `DateTime`). Ruby has no time-only or naive-time stdlib class, so **`TimeOfDay = Struct.new(:nanos_since_midnight)`** and **`NaiveTimestamp = Struct.new(:value)`** wrappers (both with a keyword-arg `initialize`, mirroring `EnumValue`'s existing precedent) carry `TIME` and `TIMESTAMP` respectively; `NaiveTimestamp`'s encode deliberately does *not* reuse `TimestampTZ`'s `t.to_r`-through-the-absolute-instant conversion — a naively-converted local-zoned `Time`'s wall-clock reading is not its UTC epoch value, so it instead reconstructs a UTC `Time` from `v.value`'s own `year`/`month`/`day`/`hour`/`min`/`sec`/`subsec` fields first (treating them as literal, ignoring whatever offset the input `Time` carries), *then* converts that to epoch nanoseconds — verified with a `+08:00`-zoned input `Time` in the test suite specifically to catch this class of mistake. `Float32`/`Float64` structs mirror `Int8`/`Uint8`; Ruby's `Array#pack`/`String#unpack1` format codes are the inverse of PHP's for float width (`'e'`=single/float32-LE, `'E'`=double/float64-LE in Ruby, versus PHP's `'g'`=float32-LE/`'e'`=double64-LE — confirmed from each language's own docs before writing either, not assumed identical). Ruby's `Integer#divmod`/`%` are also floor-based like Python's, so `KIND_TIMESTAMPTZ` decode (`ns.divmod(1_000_000_000)`) had no PHP-style bug either. Aliased at the top-level `NextSQL` module in `drivers/ruby/lib/nextsql.rb`. Tests: `drivers/ruby/test/test_protocol.rb` — `test_date_round_trip` (incl. pre-1970, `DateTime`-vs-`Date` disambiguation), `test_time_of_day_round_trip`, `test_naive_timestamp_round_trip` (the `+08:00`-zoned-input case above, and confirming a bare `Time` still defaults to `TimestampTZ`), `test_float32_float64_round_trip` (incl. NaN/Infinity) — 39/39.

100. [x] Datatype expansion D6 — `INTERVAL`, core engine + all 7 drivers + a scoping split for D9 + a scoping decision for D10, plus three real pre-existing bugs found and fixed (2026-09-04). Direct continuation of log #99: after D4/D5/D7/D8/D11's driver gaps closed under "must all datatypes must be supported end to end," the user was asked how to handle D6 (needs a design writeup)/D9 (too large, needs its own track)/D10 (needs a scoping decision) — the three remaining unstarted D-items. User picked, via `AskUserQuestion`: D6 storage = "Postgres-style 3-field storage" (over "not now" or "simple fixed-duration only"); D9 = "split into its own track now" (recommended option, confirmed after a first attempt at this question didn't capture an answer and had to be re-asked); D10 = "new GEOMETRY/GEOGRAPHY subsystem" (the larger of the two scoping options, not a generalization of the existing 4 WGS84 shapes). Given D6 was scoped as tractable (similar shape to D5) while D9/D10 are explicitly phase-sized in the docs, implemented D6 fully this session and treated D9/D10 as scoping/documentation only, reporting the split clearly rather than silently attempting open-ended phase-sized implementation without a checkpoint.

    **D9 — Collections split**: created `docs/design-collections.md` (recursive-type-descriptor scoping doc: why this is phase-sized not a Datatype-expansion bullet, relationship to existing `JSON`/`VECTOR`, a draft C1 `STRUCT`/C2 `ARRAY`/C3 `MAP` sequenced plan with each sub-item's open questions flagged for `AskUserQuestion`, explicitly deciding nothing about storage format) and a new `TODO.md` "Cross-cutting track — Collections" section mirroring the Datatype-expansion track's own structure. No code, no `Kind` constant, no catalog change.

    **D10 — Spatial scoping decision recorded**: `docs/design-datatypes.md` D10 updated to record the decision (new `GEOMETRY`/`GEOGRAPHY` subsystem, existing 4 WGS84 shapes untouched) and enumerate what a dedicated design document still needs to work out (SRID model, `GEOMETRY` vs `GEOGRAPHY` semantics, OGC Simple Features operation scope, relationship/coercion to the existing 4 types) before any `TODO.md` implementation item or code — explicitly not started, matching the same "scoped, not implemented" treatment as D9.

    **D6 — `INTERVAL` design decisions**, made while implementing (the user decided storage; every other choice below follows from that plus Postgres's own documented behavior, not invented): **on-disk layout** — `Value.IntervalMonths`/`Value.IntervalDays` (new `int32` fields) + `Value.Time` reused for nanos (same field `DATE`/`TIME`/`TIMESTAMP`/`TIMESTAMPTZ` share), 16-byte little-endian heap-row/wire encoding, no sign-bit flip (wire scalars never flip; only sortable keys do). **Comparison**: Postgres's actual `interval_cmp` "justified" rule (1 month = 30 days = 24h) — `1 month` genuinely equals `30 days`, not an approximation — implemented with explicit `int64` overflow-checking (`justifiedNanos`, erroring rather than wrapping) rather than Postgres's own wider internal arithmetic, since this engine's nanosecond precision (vs. Postgres's microseconds) makes the multiplier 1000x larger and reaches `int64` overflow within `int32` months/days's legitimate range much sooner. **Index-key ordering**: an 8-byte sign-flipped justified total, not a field-by-field encoding — field-by-field would not match `Cmp`'s order for boundary cases (`40 days` vs `1 month 10 days`), breaking index-scan/heap-scan consistency. Consequence, accepted as a deliberate tradeoff: `decodeSortable` cannot recover the exact original `(months, days)` split for an index-only-scan reconstruction, returning a canonical `(0, days, remainder-nanos)` value with the same justified total instead — the same class of canonicalization as `FLOAT`'s `-0.0` -> `+0.0` (D8), documented explicitly, not silently discovered later. A plain heap scan always returns the exact original value. **Literal syntax**: `INTERVAL 'text'` — the one D-item needing dedicated grammar, unlike D1-D5/D7/D8/D11's plain-string precedent. Not assumed upfront: originally planned to follow D5's "no new literal syntax" precedent, but the first arithmetic test (`SELECT d + INTERVAL '1 month' FROM t`) failed with "expected an expression," revealing that `evalArith`'s dispatch needs to see an actual `KindInterval`-tagged operand *before* evaluation — a bare string literal has `Kind = KindString` regardless of context, unlike column-assignment `Coerce`, which has a known destination type. Added `KwInterval` as a lexer keyword (grep-confirmed no existing test/fixture used bare `interval` as an identifier) and a `primary()` grammar production parsing `INTERVAL <string>` into an already-validated `ast.Literal` at parse time (mirroring `X'hex'`'s precedent, not `DATE`/`TIME`'s bare-string one). **`ParseInterval`/`FormatInterval`**: `"<quantity> <unit> ..."` pairs (`year(s)`/`month(s)`/`day(s)`/`hour(s)`/`minute(s)`/`second(s)`/`millisecond(s)`/`microsecond(s)`, common abbreviations); year/month/day quantities must be whole numbers (fractional calendar units are ambiguous, explicitly out of scope); hour-and-smaller accept a decimal quantity converted to nanoseconds via exact `big.Int` arithmetic (`decimalNanosFromUnit`, never float), erroring on sub-nanosecond precision rather than rounding. **Arithmetic** (`internal/executor/eval.go`, `evalIntervalArith` + helpers): `INTERVAL +/- INTERVAL` field-wise overflow-checked; `<temporal> +/- INTERVAL` for `DATE`/`TIME`/`TIMESTAMP`/`TIMESTAMPTZ`, commutative for `+`, `INTERVAL - <temporal>` rejected; `<temporal> - <same temporal>` yields `INTERVAL` (pure nanosecond-field duration, no months/days breakdown attempted — ambiguous without an anchor); unary negation. `DATE` arithmetic always promotes to `TIMESTAMP` (matches Postgres — a `DATE` has no time-of-day). Calendar-month addition (`addCalendar`) clamps day-of-month to the target month's last day (`Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28/29`) via Go `time.Time` UTC arithmetic + a `daysInMonth` helper (`time.Date(year, month+1, 0, ...)`.Day()` trick). `TIME` discards the interval's months/days (matches Postgres) and wraps modulo 24h using a sign-correct modulo (Go's `%` keeps the dividend's sign). `TIMESTAMPTZ` calendar math operates on UTC civil fields directly — this engine has no session-timezone concept, unlike Postgres's `TIMESTAMPTZ + INTERVAL`, which uses the session `timezone` GUC; a documented, deliberate simplification. `INTERVAL * scalar` (Postgres supports scaling) is explicitly out of scope for this increment — fractional-quantity distribution across calendar units is its own ambiguity, deferred rather than guessed at, the same discipline D5 used deferring all arithmetic to D6 in the first place. **Coercion**: isolated from every family but text (D1-D8 precedent). **Aggregates**: `MIN`/`MAX` free via generic `Value.Cmp`; `SUM`/`AVG` correctly error (no `INTERVAL` source case in `DECIMAL`-promotion `Coerce`). **FK eligibility**: ordinary FK-eligible scalar (block-list, not allow-list — no code change needed). **`ENCRYPTED CLIENT`**: included (`internal/clientenc/clientenc.go`) — nothing about `INTERVAL`'s fixed shape prevents opaque encryption, unlike `CHAR`'s padding or `ENUM`'s declaration-order semantics. No `NSCT` catalog version bump (`KindInterval` = 31, appended after `KindEnum` = 30).

    **Core engine, what changed**: `internal/sql/types/types.go` (`KindInterval`, `Interval()` constructor, `Comparable()`). `internal/sql/types/value.go` (`Value.IntervalMonths`/`IntervalDays` fields, `IntervalValue`/`ParseInterval`/`FormatInterval`/`justifiedNanos`/`decimalNanosFromUnit`/`parseIntervalWhole`/`intervalUnitStr` — plus the `TIMESTAMPTZ` `Coerce` fix, bug #1 below). `internal/sql/types/row.go` (`skipScalar`/`encodeScalar`/`decodeScalar`: 16-byte exact encode/decode; `encodeSortable`/`decodeSortable`: 8-byte justified-total sortable key with the canonicalizing decode documented above). `internal/sql/lexer/lexer.go` (`KwInterval` token + keyword-map entry). `internal/sql/parser/parser.go` (`colType()` case for the `INTERVAL` column-type keyword; `primary()` case for the `INTERVAL 'text'` literal). `internal/executor/eval.go` (`isTemporalKind`, `dayNanosConst`, `evalIntervalArith`, `addIntervals`, `applyIntervalToTemporal`, `addCalendar`, `daysInMonth`, `subtractTemporal`, `addInt64Checked`/`subInt64Checked`/`mulInt64Checked` overflow helpers, wired into `evalArith`'s dispatch and the unary-minus case). `internal/sql/binder/binder.go` (`facetable`). `internal/executor/idempotency.go`, `internal/catalog/workflow.go`, `internal/clientenc/clientenc.go` (the shared isolated-scalar `Kind` list, via `sed` across all three — confirmed identical resulting diff in each). `internal/xport/sql.go` (`sqlLiteral`'s quoted-text group; DDL emission needed no separate change, `sqlType` already falls through to `Type.String()`, which needed no `KindInterval` case either since `INTERVAL` has no declared-type parameters to render). `internal/executor/vector/batch.go` (`Vector.IntervalMonths`/`IntervalDays` new slice fields + `Time` reuse, wired into `newVec`/`setAt`/`getAt`/`Compact`/`clonePrefix`).

    **Bug #1 — `TIMESTAMPTZ` had no string-literal coercion path, predating this entire track.** `internal/sql/types/value.go`'s `Coerce` had no `case KindTimestampTZ:` in its destination-Kind-differs switch at all; `ParseTimestamp` (`internal/sql/types/value.go`) was fully implemented but grep-confirmed never called from anywhere outside its own definition and tests. Every existing test in the whole codebase populates `TIMESTAMPTZ` via `DEFAULT NOW()` or a driver-native datetime object sent directly as `Kind.TimestampTZ` over the wire (bypassing text coercion), confirmed by grep across `internal/executor/*_test.go` finding zero instances of a string literal INSERT into a `TIMESTAMPTZ` column anywhere. Found only because `TestIntervalTimestampArithmetic` needed a `TIMESTAMPTZ` column populated by literal text to combine with `INTERVAL`; reproduced in complete isolation via a throwaway debug test (removed before landing) before concluding it was real and not a test-authoring mistake. Fixed by adding `case KindTimestampTZ: if textlike(...) { return ParseTimestamp(...) }`, the exact same isolated-text-coercion shape `DATE`/`TIME`/`TIMESTAMP` already used.

    **Bug #2 — `FormatInterval`/`ParseInterval` were not round-trippable**, despite `FormatInterval`'s own doc comment (written in the same session, moments earlier) explicitly claiming they were. `FormatInterval` originally rendered the time component as `HH:MM:SS[.frac]` (colon-separated), but `ParseInterval`'s actual grammar only understands `"<quantity> <unit>"` pairs and has zero colon-time handling. Caught immediately by `TestIntervalParseFormat`'s own format-then-reparse assertion, before this ever left the session, let alone shipped — exactly the kind of thing a round-trip test exists to catch. Fixed by rewriting `FormatInterval`'s time-component output to `"<n> hours <n> minutes <n[.frac]> seconds"`, the same shape `ParseInterval` parses; the now-dead `pad2` helper (only used by the old colon formatting) was removed rather than left as unused code.

    **Bug #3 — Node driver's `putU64` threw on negative `BigInt`, silently pre-broken for pre-1970 `TIMESTAMPTZ`/`TIMESTAMP` too.** `drivers/node/nextsql.js`'s `putU64` called `Buffer.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n), 0)` directly; Node's `Buffer.writeBigUInt64LE` requires its argument in `[0, 2^64)` and throws a `RangeError` for anything negative — verified directly (`b.writeBigUInt64LE(-5n, 0)` throws `"must be >= 0n and < 2n ** 64n"`) — unlike the shared JS/Bun/Deno driver's `DataView.setBigUint64`, which wraps a negative `BigInt` to its unsigned two's-complement bit pattern automatically per the ECMAScript `ToBigUint64` abstract operation (confirmed: `BigInt.asUintN` exists specifically to replicate that wrapping). This function is also what `encodeTimestamp`/`encodeNaiveTimestamp` use for `TIMESTAMPTZ`/`TIMESTAMP`'s epoch-nanosecond encoding, so every pre-1970 value encoded through the Node driver specifically (not JS/Bun/Deno, which share the already-correct `protocol.mjs`) has been silently broken since D5/D7 shipped — undetected because the existing Node test suite's own pre-1970 case (`preEpoch` in the D4/D5/D7/D8 test) exercises `DATE`, which uses a completely different `int32` `writeInt32LE` encode path that never touches `putU64` at all; nothing exercised a negative value through `putU64` specifically until this `INTERVAL` test (`nanos: -3_600_000_000_000n`). Fixed with `BigInt.asUintN(64, BigInt(n))` before the `Buffer` write; added as an explicit regression-test comment in `drivers/node/nextsql.test.js`, not just a passing assertion, so the "why" survives future edits.

101. [x] Aggregation fast path counted un-purged committed tombstones on a partitioned heap — `SELECT COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY` and `SELECT COUNT(*)` could over-report row counts after concurrent DELETE churn (2026-09-04). Fixing the pre-existing failing regression test flagged in logs #99/#100 (`TestPartitionCrossPartitionUniqueSustainedConcurrentWrites`, `internal/executor/partition_test.go`, committed with debug instrumentation in `4efc687`). **Not** a cross-partition UNIQUE bug despite the test's name and the earlier `partition.go` `SetName` work: the UNIQUE probe and its engine-global key lock (`LockManager.Acquire` keys on the raw key bytes, not the tree tag, so `SetName` is display-only) correctly serialize sibling-partition writers; the heap and the UNIQUE index were consistent the whole time. The wrong answer came from the read side. `partitionWiseHeapAggregate` / `streamHeapAggregate` / `parallelHeapAggregate` / `parallelCountLive` (`internal/executor/exec_vector.go`) take a fast path when `soleSnapshot()` is true — `btree.Txn.RangeLive` / `RangeLiveRange` / `CountLiveRange` — that skips the per-row MVCC visibility check. Those three btree walks (`rangeLiveLocked`, the `skipVis` branch of `rangeCount`, and the `skipVis` branch of `visitLeaf`) iterated **every physically-present slot**, including committed tombstones that the deleting transaction could not reclaim at commit because a concurrent snapshot still needed them — so a deleted row that had not yet been VACUUMed was counted as live. Masked in normal use because a sole-writer DELETE purges its own tombstone immediately (`xact.commit` → `PurgeDeleted`); the sustained 4-writer INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE workload defeats that, then the trailing single-reader aggregate hits the fast path and counts the residue. Inconsistent with the rest of the "Live" family — `page.LiveSlots()` / `Tree.liveRows` / `countLiveLocked` (used by `CountLive()`) all already exclude tombstones. **Fix**: the three `skipVis`/`skipTomb` walks now skip records whose version carries a committed `Xmax` (`ver.Xmax != 0`; under the sole-snapshot precondition that unambiguously means "delete committed"). `rangeLiveLocked` took a `skipTomb bool` param so the raw physical walk is still available: `RangeLive` passes `true`, a new `Txn.RangePhysical` passes `false` for maintenance / VACUUM verification (`physicalRows` test helper in `internal/executor/maintenance_test.go` switched to it — it deliberately wants to see deferred tombstones). No on-disk format, wire, or catalog change; no isolation-level or MVCC-correctness change (the non-fast `Range`/`RangeVisible` path was already correct — confirmed by forcing it and watching the test pass). **Test**: the flagged test's throwaway `t.Logf("DEBUG …")` lines are replaced with real assertions — `COUNT(*)` must equal the heap-scan row count, and `GROUP BY email` must sum to the same total with no more groups than rows — so the aggregate-vs-heap consistency this bug broke is now a permanent regression guard. Verified: target test 5/5 under `-race`; `internal/executor` full package green (incl. all `TestMaintain*` / `TestCleanupDeadVersions*` that exercise deferred-tombstone behavior); `internal/storage/btree`, `internal/storage/...`, `internal/recovery`, `internal/wal`, `tests/integration` green; `go build ./...` / `go vet` clean. `CHANGELOG.md` updated (this is a shipped correctness fix, unlike the docs-only reconciliations of #96-#100). Everything uncommitted, per the standing repo convention.

Logs #104/#105 built the non-interactive backbone for bringing a server *up* and for the read-only lifecycle queries (detect/preflight/backup-config); this increment is the one mutating command they left open — apply an in-place format upgrade under this binary — still with no UI-framework decision on the critical path. **What an in-place upgrade means for NextSQL**: catalog/format migration is lazy (old descriptors decode, re-encode on next write) and WAL recovery runs at every engine open, so there is no separate "migrator" to invoke. The runner's job is to make that first open happen *deliberately and observed*: hold the deployment lock so no `nextsqld` races in, confirm this binary can open the store at all (preflight), take a verified config backup, then open the encrypted store once — running WAL recovery (the actual on-disk change) and confirming the catalog decodes under the new format code while the operator is still watching, not at 3 a.m. on the first client connection — and re-verify the plaintext headers afterward. **New pure logic in `internal/setup/lifecycle.go` (no I/O)**: `UpgradePlan(UpgradePlanInput{ConfigPresent}) → []UpgradeStep` — the ordered steps (`acquire-deployment-lock`, `preflight`, `backup-config` (only when a config exists), `open-engine`, `re-verify`), each flagged `Mutates`, so the `--dry-run` output and the eventual GUI installer's "staged progress" (an open P28 UX item) come from one source; `UpgradeOutcome` (`applied`/`dry-run`/`blocked`/`failed-verify`). **New `nextsql lifecycle upgrade`** (`cmd/nextsql/lifecycle.go`, wired into the `lifecycleCmd` switch + `main.go` usage) — `--data-dir --key-file [--config FILE] [--buffer-pages N] [--dry-run] [--json]`. Flow: stat data-dir (missing → `blocked`/not-initialized, exit 7) → `hosting.AcquireDataDirLock` **held for the whole operation** via `defer lock.Close()` (`nerr.Unavailable` → `blocked`/server-running, exit 2) → `assessInPlaceUpgrade(dataDir, lockHeld=false)` (we hold the lock, so no server) → non-`ready` verdict → `blocked` (exit 2/6/7, nothing mutated) → `--dry-run` → print plan + verdict, `outcome=dry-run`, exit 0, mutate nothing → `backupConfigFile` verified copy (failure → `failed-verify` exit 5, the written copy is retained and its path reported) → `openEnvelope` + `executor.Open` with `--buffer-pages` (default `config.DefaultBufferPages`); open failure → `failed-verify` exit 5 → capture table count + durable LSN, `db.Close()` → `assessInPlaceUpgrade` again; still not OK → `failed-verify` exit 5 → `outcome=applied`, exit 0. **Never deletes anything on any path**; does not swap the `nextsqld` binary or restart a service (the OS installer / operator does that around this call); idempotent (a second run just opens again and reports `applied`). `--json` emits one object (plan steps, assessment, config-backup path + verified flag, engine-open result, summary). **Refactors** (no behavior change to the existing subcommands): `lifecyclePreflight`'s inline `upgrade.Report` → `[]FamilyCheck` → `AssessUpgrade` mapping extracted to `assessInPlaceUpgrade(dataDir, lockHeld)`; `lifecycleBackupConfig`'s read→parse→atomic-copy→reload-and-compare extracted to `backupConfigFile(op, src, outDir) (backupConfigResult, error)` — both now shared with `upgrade`. `lifecycleBackupConfig` re-expressed on top of the helper (still emits JSON on the unverified-copy error path). **Docs**: `docs/install.md` — new "`nextsql lifecycle upgrade`" section (ordered steps, outcome/exit table, "does not swap the binary or restart a service", idempotent), "still to come" narrowed to `repair`/`uninstall`/rolling-cluster/rollback/GUI/Manager; `internal/setup` (19 existing + 2 new `UpgradePlan` tests = 21), `cmd/nextsql` setup+lifecycle (16 existing + 5 new `upgrade` tests = 21: dry-run mutates nothing, applies+verifies+leaves a config backup + idempotent second run, missing `--key-file` → 7, not-initialized → 7, deployment-lock-held → 2) pass incl. `-race`; Storage caps (`NSRM` v3, log in the M3 "Registry storage caps" line) landed write-path enforcement but left "advisory `system.quotas` surfacing" as an explicit follow-on — until now the only signal that a database is near/over its cap was the write-path `nerr.Exhausted` rejection itself. **What landed**: a read-only `system.quotas` virtual table, admin-only and empty on a legacy/non-hosted deployment (`s.hostingRegistry == nil`), exactly the same convention as `system.realms`/`system.databases` (M2-4a). One row per realm (`scope='realm'`, empty `database_name`) and one per database (`scope='database'`) from `hosting.Registry.Manifest()`. Columns: `scope, realm_name, database_name, state, cap_bytes, effective_cap_bytes, usage_known, used_bytes, pct_of_cap, over_cap`. `cap_bytes` is that scope's own configured cap (0 = none); `effective_cap_bytes` is `hosting.EffectiveStorageCapBytes(realmCap, dbCap)` for a database row and the realm cap for a realm row. **Usage columns** (`used_bytes`, `pct_of_cap` as an integer percent, `over_cap`) are populated **only for the row matching the session's own connected realm+database** — matched on `s.realmID` against `manifest.Realms[].ID` and `s.db.DatabaseName()` against the database name — because no other database's engine is reachable from a single connection; every other row has `usage_known = false` and zeroed usage. `used_bytes = uint64(s.db.Eng.Alloc.Next()) * PhysicalPageSize`, the data-file logical high-water — the exact quantity the allocator cap (`next >= capPages`) is enforced against, so `over_cap` here agrees with the write-path rejection. The view never errors and never bounds anything. **Design decisions**: (1) new virtual table rather than columns on `system.databases` — keeps the pure-registry `system.databases` stable and separates "durable operator intent" from "live advisory usage"; (2) per-realm aggregate usage / cross-database roll-up / "N% of cap" metrics / over-cap alerts explicitly left as follow-ons (a single connection can't see sibling databases' engines); (3) `SchemaVersion` NOT bumped — the documented rule is "bump only when a `system.*` table's *columns* change shape", and this only adds a table; discovery is via the new `system.capabilities` row `quotas_view` (`supported`), matching how `storage_caps`/`resource_groups` are surfaced. **Files**: `internal/system/schema.go` (`register("quotas", …)` + `rowCap("quotas_view", …)`), `internal/executor/system.go` (`case "system.quotas"` + `systemQuotasRows`), `internal/executor/hosting_system_test.go` (`TestSystemQuotasViewNilRegistry` — empty on legacy; `TestSystemQuotasViewRBACAndContent` — non-admin sees zero rows, admin sees 1 realm + 2 database rows, realm cap 100 MiB / db1 cap 40 MiB → db1 `effective_cap_bytes` 40 MiB and db2 (uncapped) inherits the 100 MiB realm cap, `usage_known` true only for the connected `acme/db1` with positive `used_bytes` and `over_cap` false). **Docs**: `docs/design-multidatabase-dbaas.md` §10.1 (the "Advisory surfacing" paragraph rewritten from "separate follow-on" to the landed shape), `docs/system-catalog.md` (new "Multi-database hosting" section documenting `system.realms`/`system.databases`/`system.quotas` — the first two were previously undocumented there), this TODO.md M3 line + entry, `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`. **Verify**: `go build ./...` + `go vet ./...` clean; `internal/executor` (`-run TestSystemQuotas|TestSystemHostingViews`) + `internal/system` green; full `internal/executor` package green. Everything uncommitted, per the standing repo convention. **Concurrent sessions**: `nextsql-88` on Spatial S1 (taking its own next log number), `nextsql-fa` on the P28 installer track — all file-disjoint from this change bar surgical TODO.md/CHANGELOG edits.

New `security.ActionDatabaseSuspend`/`ActionDatabaseResume` audit actions, logged via the existing `auditLocal` helper (`create`'s own precedent; `set-realm-cap`/`set-database-cap`/`set-realm-root` do not currently audit — a pre-existing gap, noted, not retrofitted here). **Tests**: `internal/hosting/create_test.go` — `TestLookupRejectsNonActiveDatabaseState` (table across all five non-Active states, exact code + message substring per state), `TestLookupRejectsNonActiveRealm` (suspended realm blocks an Active database inside it); `TestLookupResolvesRealmAndDatabaseCaseInsensitively` updated to activate the database before asserting `Lookup` success — it previously passed by resolving a still-`StateProvisioning` database, i.e. it was accidentally exercising the exact bug this increment closes, not the name-normalization behavior it's named for. `cmd/nextsql/realm_database_test.go` — `TestDatabaseSuspendResumeCLI` (missing `--confirm` for both verbs, deployment-lock rejection, unknown-realm rejection, and — the enforcement proof, not just persistence — a real `hosting.Registry.Lookup` call against the on-disk registry rejecting the suspended pair with `Unavailable` and succeeding again once resumed). 113. [x] **Spatial track — S1 through S6, `GEOMETRY`/`GEOGRAPHY` end to end** (2026-09-04). NOT a Phase 0–28 item — the Spatial cross-cutting track (D10, `docs/design-spatial.md`), the counterpart to the Collections track (log #109). User: "implement Collections and Spatial" → "must be full" → `AskUserQuestion` "finish Collections fully, then start Spatial" → this session wrote `docs/design-spatial.md` + S1's type skeleton, reported status, then the user said "implement that end to end" / "continue", driving S1 through S6 to completion in one continuous session. **Design decisions** (full record in `docs/design-spatial.md` §2): `GEOMETRY` (planar/Cartesian) and `GEOGRAPHY` (geodetic, defaults SRID 4326) are separate `Kind`s (35/36), not one type with a flag; SRID + OGC subtype are a **per-column declaration** (`GEOMETRY(Point, 3857)`) carried in the existing `Type.Precision`/`Type.Scale` fields — **no `NSCT` or NSQL protocol version bump**, same precedent as every scalar D-item; SRID registry is the closed set `{0, 4326, 3857}`, `ST_Transform` covers only `4326↔3857` via closed-form spherical Mercator math (no `PROJ`/`proj4` dependency, matching `docs/geo.md`'s "not a GIS sidecar" stance); on-disk is EWKB with a `u32` total-length prefix (O(1) `skipScalar` at any nesting depth, same shape as the Collections track's nested encoding); index-key/`=`/`ORDER BY` order is canonical-EWKB byte order — a deterministic total order, explicitly *not* geometrically meaningful (documented, matches PostGIS's own `ORDER BY geom` pragmatism); the four fixed WGS84 types (`docs/geo.md`) are **completely unchanged** and coerce into/out of `GEOMETRY`/`GEOGRAPHY` implicitly (NextSQL has no `CAST(x AS type)` SQL syntax — coercion is `types.Coerce`, driven by column-assignment/function-argument context, same as every other type in this engine). **S1 (types + codec + plumbing)**: `internal/sql/types/spatial.go` (new file) — `Geom` recursive value struct (`Type`, `SRID`, `Coords`, `Rings`, `Parts`), `EncodeEWKB`/`DecodeEWKB` (depth/part/vertex-bounded, per `MaxSpatialDepth`=8/`MaxSpatialParts`=4096/`MaxSpatialVertices`=65536), `ParseGeneralWKT`/`FormatGeomWKT`/`FormatGeomEWKT` (WKT/EWKT incl. `SRID=n;` prefix, all 7 OGC subtypes), `canonicalizeGeom` (closes rings, normalizes exterior-CCW/hole-CW orientation — a degenerate zero-area ring is left untouched so canonicalization stays idempotent, a real bug found via fuzz and fixed), heap-row (`encodeGeneralGeo`/`decodeGeneralGeo`) + sortable-key (`encodeSortableGeneralGeo`/`decodeSortableGeneralGeo`) hooks wired into `row.go`'s existing switches, `Value.Geom` field (+ `Clone`), `Cmp`/`Coerce`/`String` cases in `value.go`, `Comparable()` in `types.go`. Lexer (`GEOMETRY`/`GEOGRAPHY` keywords), parser (`geoTypeArgs` — `(subtype[, srid])`, subtype names shared with `types.GeomSubByName`), binder (`IsSpatialFunc` allowlist alongside the existing `IsGeoFunc`), new `internal/executor/eval_spatial.go` (`evalSpatialFn`, checked before `types.EvalGeo` so a general-geometry operand is handled here and a fixed-shape operand falls through unchanged — the two families share `ST_X`/`ST_Y`/`ST_GeometryType`/etc. by argument-type dispatch, not by name partition), `internal/executor/vector/batch.go` (`Vector.Geom []*types.Geom`), FK block-list (`internal/catalog/fk.go`), workflow param allowlist (`internal/catalog/workflow.go`), `xport` (`ST_GeomFromEWKT('SRID=..;...')` / `ST_GeogFromText('...')` re-insertable literals). `ENCRYPTED CLIENT` needs no new exclusion (`clientenc` is already a `KindString`-only allow-list). **S2 (measurement + predicates)**: new `internal/sql/types/spatial_ops.go` — planar primitives (`planarDist`, `planarPointSeg`, `pointInPolygon` reusing `geo.go`'s existing `pointInRingState`), `GeomDistance`/`GeomLength`/`GeomPerimeter`/`GeomArea`/`GeomCentroid` (geodetic branch reuses `geo.go`'s `haversine`/`sphericalRingArea`), `GeomsIntersect`/`GeomContains`/`GeomEquals` (native semantics: vertex+segment-midpoint containment test, not full DE-9IM — documented in `docs/design-spatial.md` §8), `ST_Transform` (closed-form spherical Mercator, `TransformGeom`). **S3 (spatial index)**: `internal/executor/exec.go` `indexKV`'s spatial branch now accepts `GEOMETRY`/`GEOGRAPHY` (keys on the value's bbox centre, reusing the existing `GeoHash64`/`EncodeGeoKey` Z-order machinery); `internal/sql/optimizer/physical.go` — new `geoConstGeom`/`geoGeneralColConst` recognize a constant `ST_GeomFromText`/`ST_Point`/WKT-string argument and extend `oneSpatial`'s existing `dwithin`/`within` matching to the general family; `cost.go` selectivity estimation. **Real bug found and fixed**: a `GEOMETRY` column's `ST_DWithin(col, const, r)` radius is in the column's own planar coordinate units, not metres, but the existing `ExpandBBox` helper (built for the metres-based fixed-`POINT` case) always converts via a metres→degrees approximation — a `1.5`-unit radius was silently expanded by only ~1.5mm. Fixed with a new `spatialMatch.planar` flag that expands the bbox directly in coordinate units for a `GEOMETRY` column. **S4 (drivers, all 7)**: `drivers/js/protocol.mjs` (shared by Bun/Deno) and `drivers/node/nextsql.js` each gained `Kind.Geometry`/`Kind.Geography` (35/36) and a recursive EWKB decoder (`decodeEWKB`) producing a GeoJSON-shaped `{type, srid, coordinates}` object, plus `geoToWKT` so a decoded value can be sent straight back; `drivers/python/nextsql/protocol.py` (`Geometry` dataclass with `.to_wkt()`), `drivers/php/src/Protocol.php` (`decodeEWKB`/`geoToWKT` static methods), `drivers/ruby/lib/nextsql/protocol.rb` (`Geometry` struct with `#to_wkt`) mirror the same shape. Every driver's param path: a plain WKT/EWKT string already round-trips (the server coerces `STRING` into the destination column, same as every fixed geo type); an explicit `{kind:'geometry'|'geography', wkt, srid}` wrapper (or `Geometry.new(wkt:, srid:)` in Ruby/Python) is also accepted. **S5 (overlay operators)**, `spatial_ops.go` continued: `GeomConvexHull` (exact, Andrew's monotone chain), `GeomSimplify` (exact, Douglas–Peucker against a point-to-segment distance tolerance), `GeomSegmentize` (exact, linear interpolation), `GeomBuffer` (exact circle-polygon for a Point; for anything else, the convex hull of every vertex's own offset-circle point cloud — a documented convex over-approximation, never an under-approximation, since a true Minkowski-sum buffer of a concave shape is a substantially harder problem deliberately not attempted), `GeomIntersection` (Sutherland–Hodgman clipping, exact when at least one polygon operand is convex, a clear error otherwise), `GeomUnion`/`GeomDifference` (exact for the disjoint and containment-nesting cases, a clear error for two general overlapping non-convex polygons) — **all four explicitly refuse to guess at a general polygon-boolean result** rather than return a silently wrong boundary, per `CLAUDE.md`'s correctness-over-features priority order; a full Vatti/Greiner–Hormann general polygon-clipping algorithm (with hole and self-intersection handling) is flagged in `docs/design-spatial.md` §8 as a genuinely separate, substantial computational-geometry subproject, not attempted partially. **Real bug found and fixed**: the Sutherland–Hodgman line-intersection formula's denominator had the wrong sign (`edx*dy - edy*dx` instead of `dx*edy - dy*edx`), which flipped every computed intersection parameter `t` and produced wildly wrong clip polygons (caught by a known-area assertion — two overlapping 4×4 squares should intersect to area 4, produced 24 — not by a fuzz target, since the bug was a systematic sign error, not an edge case). **S6 (GeoJSON + docs)**: `ParseGeoJSON`/`GeomToGeoJSON` (RFC 7946, stdlib `encoding/json`) in `spatial.go`, wired as `ST_GeomFromGeoJSON`/`ST_AsGeoJSON` in `eval_spatial.go`. **Two real crash bugs found by `FuzzParseGeoJSON` and fixed**: (1) `canonicalizeGeom` indexed into a polygon ring's first/last coordinate before `validateGeom` had confirmed the ring was non-empty, so a zero-length ring (`"coordinates":[[]]`) panicked with an index-out-of-range instead of failing closed with a clean error — fixed by validating ring length during GeoJSON parsing itself (mirroring the WKT parser's own precedent of validating during parse, not after); (2) `flattenXY` silently *dropped* any GeoJSON position with fewer than 2 coordinates instead of erroring, so a ring reported as having (e.g.) 4 raw positions could end up with fewer than 4 actual coordinate pairs after flattening — a ring-count/coordinate-count mismatch that also fed the first bug — fixed by making `flattenXY` fail closed on a short position rather than silently shrinking the ring. `ST_Collect`/`ST_Extent` aggregates **explicitly deferred**, not attempted: NextSQL's aggregate framework (`COUNT`/`SUM`/`AVG`/`MIN`/`MAX`) is a hardcoded name list spanning the binder's aggregate detection, `GROUP BY` planning, and the hash-aggregate executor — a new aggregate function class is a separable cross-cutting change comparable in shape to the Collections track's own `ARRAY_AGG` deferral (log #109), not a scalar-function addition, and starting it speculatively inside this track would contradict the "smallest coherent increment" discipline. **Tests**: `internal/sql/types/spatial_test.go` (`TestSpatialWKTEWKBRoundTrip` incl. every OGC subtype, `TestSpatialEWKTPrefix`, `TestSpatialSubtypeAndSRIDEnforced`, `TestSpatialCastBridge`, `TestSpatialTextCoerce`, `TestSpatialDecodeEWKBBounds`, `TestSpatialOps` — area/perimeter/intersects/contains/distance/centroid incl. a hole-subtracted polygon and a geodetic 1°×1° box, `TestSpatialS5` — hull/simplify/segmentize/buffer/intersection/union/difference), `internal/sql/types/spatial_fuzz_test.go` (`FuzzParseGeneralWKT`, `FuzzDecodeEWKB`, `FuzzParseGeoJSON` — all multi-million-exec clean after the fixes above), `internal/executor/spatial_test.go` (`TestSpatialS1`..`TestSpatialS5`, `TestSpatialS6GeoJSON` — full `CREATE TABLE`/constructor/accessor/predicate/index/restart coverage against a real encrypted engine, not just in-process type-layer tests). Every official driver's own suite gained a spatial EWKB round-trip test. **Verify**: `go build ./...` (repo-wide, excluding the unrelated concurrent `cmd/nextsql` churn from other sessions) + `go vet ./internal/sql/... ./internal/executor/...` clean; `internal/sql/types`, `internal/sql/parser`, `internal/sql/binder`, `internal/sql/optimizer`, `internal/catalog`, `internal/protocol`, `internal/xport`, `internal/executor` (~70s), `tests/integration` all green; all three spatial fuzz targets multi-million-exec clean; all 7 drivers' own test suites green (Bun 25/25, Deno 25/25, Node 27/27, Python 44/44, PHP `unit.php` ok, Ruby 43/43). Docs: `docs/design-spatial.md` (§7 status table, §8 deferred-scope additions), `docs/geo.md` (cross-reference to the general family), `docs/sql.md` (`GEOMETRY`/`GEOGRAPHY` type-table rows), `PROJECT.md` §29 (rewritten to describe both spatial families), `docs/design-datatypes.md` D10 (already pointed at this track from log #109's session), `TODO.md` (this entry + all six S-item checklist boxes), `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`. **Concurrent sessions**: `nextsql-fa` (P28 installer track, logs #104–#110) and the M3-hosting session (logs #111–#112) were both active throughout — coordinated via `SendMessage` at the start of this track and again when M3 picked up; both stayed file-disjoint from `internal/sql/types/*`, `internal/sql/{lexer,parser,binder,optimizer}`, `internal/executor/eval*.go`/`exec.go`'s spatial branch, `internal/executor/vector/batch.go`, `internal/xport/sql.go`, `internal/catalog/{fk,workflow}.go`, all 7 `drivers/*`, and this track's own doc/TODO/CHANGELOG sections. Idempotent and crash-resumable at every step: an already-`StateTombstoned` database reports success without erroring (a prior run may have reclaimed the files but crashed before the final state write); `StateDeleting → StateDeleting` is a valid no-op transition (`CanTransition`'s same-state rule), so a run that crashed after the first state write but before reclaiming files resumes cleanly on retry (`os.RemoveAll` on an already-gone directory is itself a no-op, not an error). 115. [x] **Spatial track — two real predicate bugs found and fixed by a dedicated bug-hunt pass** (2026-09-04). Continuing on log #113 (Spatial S1–S6) after the user said "fix all bugs" — read that as "verify there's nothing else lurking in the freshest code," not a request to re-litigate already-closed items (checked first: `TestPartitionCrossPartitionUniqueSustainedConcurrentWrites` 3/3 clean under `-race`, `rebuild_index_online` still `"supported"` — both were flagged unfixed in *older* log entries but already closed by later ones, log #101/#93; the one genuinely open item, "local commit precedes replication acknowledgment"'s narrow ambiguous/in-doubt residual case, is a deliberate, structurally-undecidable, already-mitigated design tradeoff per log #79/#68, not a bug to fix). Targeted the newest, least-directly-tested code instead: the S2 predicate suite's `ST_Touches`/`ST_Contains`, which had never been unit-tested against *self*-comparison (identical or coincident-boundary geometries) — a gap the earlier fuzz/known-area tests couldn't catch, since fuzzing checks crash-safety and structural round-trips, not predicate correctness against a hand-computed expected answer. **Bug 1 — `ST_Touches(A, A)` returned `true` for two identical polygons** (should be `false`: touching requires disjoint interiors, but two identical shapes have fully coincident, not disjoint, interiors). Root cause: `st_touches` used `GeomContains(a,b,covers=false)` (strict) on both sides to rule out containment, but strict containment requires a sample point (vertex or edge-midpoint) landing *strictly inside* the other polygon — for two identical squares, every sampled point of B lies exactly on A's shared boundary, so strict-contains never fires, and the identical pair fell through as "touching." **Fix**: `st_touches` now uses `GeomContains(_, _, covers=true)` on both sides (`internal/executor/eval_spatial.go`) — covers-containment only needs every point in-or-on, which correctly fires for the identical case (and still correctly stays false for a true edge-adjacent pair, verified). **Bug 2 — `ST_Contains(A, A)` returned `false`** (a polygon does not contain an identical copy of itself, which is wrong — self-containment is a basic OGC guarantee, and PostGIS returns true). Same root cause from the other side: vertex/edge-midpoint sampling of B against A can *never* find a strictly-interior point when B's entire boundary coincides with A's, because every one of those sample points is definitionally on the boundary, not the interior — this isn't specific to A==B, it's any B whose boundary sample set happens to lie entirely on A's boundary. **Fix**: `GeomContains` (`internal/sql/types/spatial_ops.go`) now also probes the centroid of each polygonal part of B as a candidate strictly-interior point when the vertex/edge-midpoint samples found none — a solid polygon's own centroid is virtually always strictly inside its own body, so this reliably resolves the self/coincident-boundary case without weakening the existing checks (verified: strict containment of a genuinely non-overlapping neighbor is still correctly false, and the `ST_Touches` fix still correctly returns true for real edge-adjacent polygons and false for the identical case, together). Both fixes verified consistent with each other and with `ST_Equals`/`ST_Within`/`ST_CoveredBy` (which were already correct — `covers=true` self-comparison and `lineCoversGeom`'s LineString path were unaffected by either bug). **Tests**: `internal/sql/types/spatial_test.go` `TestSpatialPredicateSelfCases` (new: `ST_Contains(A,A)` true, strictly-interior-B true, non-overlapping-neighbor false; `ST_Touches(A,A)` false, edge-adjacent true) — a permanent regression guard for exactly this bug class. Live-verified through real SQL (`ST_Touches`/`ST_Contains`/`ST_Equals` on two identical `ST_GeomFromText` polygons via a real encrypted engine, not just the type-layer). **Verify**: `go build ./internal/...` clean; `internal/sql/types` (incl. `-fuzz FuzzParseGeneralWKT` 20s clean, confirming the fix didn't regress the WKT/EWKB round-trip path) and `internal/executor` (71s) full packages green. No format/protocol change — pure algorithm fix in already-landed S2 code. Docs: this entry (no `design-spatial.md`/`CHANGELOG.md` rewrite — the S2 status line in `docs/design-spatial.md` §7 already just says "landed," and these are bug fixes within that landed scope, not a new increment or a behavior addition worth its own changelog bullet beyond this log). 116. [x] **FROM-less `SELECT` support (e.g. `SELECT 1`, `SELECT NOW()`)** (2026-09-04). Continuing "continue @TODO.md" → user said "fix it" in response to log #114's incidental finding: `internal/sql/parser/parser.go`'s `sel()` unconditionally required `FROM`, so `CLAUDE.md`'s own "Run locally" quickstart (`nextsql exec ... -c "SELECT 1"`) could not run as documented. Chose the smallest coherent shape given NextSQL's SELECT pipeline is deeply table-centric (`bindSelect` is 362 lines of schema-qualified join/aggregate machinery with no "no relation" concept, and there is no existing standalone `VALUES`/`DUAL`-style single-row source to reuse): a parser-level `ast.Select.NoFrom` flag plus a dedicated executor bypass, mirroring the **already-existing architectural precedent** of `system.*` virtual tables (`isSystemSelect`/`execSystemSelect`, `internal/executor/system.go`) — both bypass the normal binder/planner/catalog pipeline entirely and evaluate `ast.Expr`s directly via the raw-AST evaluator `Session.eval(expr, tab, row)`, which already handled `tab == nil` cleanly for every relevant case (`ast.Ident`/`ast.Path` column references error `"column reference is not valid in this context"`, literals/function calls/arithmetic need no table at all) — discovered by reading `eval.go` rather than assumed. **Parser** (`internal/sql/parser/parser.go` `sel()`): `FROM` is now optional — `if p.tok.Kind == lexer.KwFrom { ...unchanged table/derived-table/JOIN parsing... } else if s.Star { error "expected FROM" } else { s.NoFrom = true }`, so `SELECT *` (which needs a table to expand) is unaffected and still requires `FROM`; the existing `joinsDone:` goto-label target is unchanged (Go permits a label after a block a nested `goto` jumps out to). `WHERE`/`ORDER BY`/`LIMIT`/`OFFSET` remain syntactically available and meaningful against the single synthetic row (`SELECT 1 WHERE 1=0` returns zero rows); a trailing check rejects `NoFrom` combined with `GROUP BY`/`HAVING`/`SEARCH`/`NEAREST`/`FACET` (all fundamentally need a table or index) with a clear syntax error rather than an indirect downstream "unknown table" one. New `ast.Select.NoFrom bool` field (`internal/sql/ast/ast.go`), documented as always paired with empty `Table`/nil `FromQuery`/empty `Joins`. **Executor** (`internal/executor/no_from_select.go`, new file): `isNoFromSelect` (defense-in-depth structural re-check, matching `isSystemSelect`'s own style) + `execNoFromSelect` — evaluates `sel.Where` against `(nil, nil)` to decide 0-vs-1 rows, evaluates each `sel.List` item the same way for the projected row, validates (but does not need to sort) `sel.Order` expressions so a bad column reference there still errors rather than being silently ignored, applies `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` trivially to the at-most-one row (DISTINCT needs no handling — a single row is already distinct). Wired into `Session.exec` (`internal/executor/session.go`) as a new early-return branch immediately before the existing `isSystemSelect` check, same shape: `s.auditRecord(workflowAuditAction(stmt), sqlObject(stmt), err)` then return, bypassing `s.authorize` entirely (there is no object to check a privilege against — computing `1+1` needs no RBAC any more than it needs a table). Column-name defaulting (`?` for a bare expression with no alias, the call name for a bare function call) factored into a shared `selectListNames` helper mirroring `execSystemSelect`'s own inline projection-naming logic. **Explicitly out of scope, noted not silently assumed**: `EXPLAIN SELECT 1` still goes through the normal binder (`internal/sql/binder/binder.go`'s `case ast.Explain:` calls `bind()` directly, independent of this bypass) and gets a `mustTable(lookup, "")`-shaped "unknown table" error rather than a real explain plan — not a crash, just an unimplemented combination; result caching (`selectIsVolatile`) never sees a `NoFrom` select since the bypass runs earlier, which is fine (nothing here is expensive enough to need caching). **Tests**: `internal/sql/parser/parser_test.go` — `TestParseSelectNoFrom` (AST shape for a bare select and one with every allowed clause), `TestParseSelectStarRequiresFrom`, `TestParseSelectNoFromRejectsTableOnlyClauses` (`GROUP BY`/`HAVING`/`SEARCH`/`FACET`); `internal/sql/parser/fuzz_test.go` — 4 new `FuzzParse` seeds exercising the new code path (8 s / 1M+ execs clean, no new crashes). `internal/executor/no_from_select_test.go` — `TestNoFromSelect`: literal projection + aliases (`SELECT 1 AS x, 2+2 AS y, 'hi' AS z`), `NOW()`/`UUID()` (no table needed), `WHERE` true/false, `LIMIT 0`/`OFFSET 1` (both → zero rows), a bare column reference and `ORDER BY` of one both fail closed (`invalid_argument`, not silently accepted), `SELECT *` and `GROUP BY` still require `FROM` (`syntax`), and a real table-backed `SELECT ... FROM t` is unaffected end to end. **Verify**: `go build ./...` / `go vet ./...` clean repo-wide; `internal/sql/parser`, `internal/sql/binder`, `internal/sql/optimizer`, `internal/sql/types` green; `internal/executor` full package green under `-race` (139 s, incl. `aggregate`/`join`/`sort`/`vector` subpackages); `tests/integration` green (26.6 s). **Live-verified end to end** against real `nextsql`/`nextsqld` binaries, reproducing `CLAUDE.md`'s exact documented quickstart command byte-for-byte (`nextsql init` → `nextsqld --listen 127.0.0.1:PORT` → `nextsql exec --addr ... --insecure -c "SELECT 1"`) — previously failed with `nextsql: nextsql syntax: nextsql: expected FROM`, now returns column `?` / row `1`. **Docs**: `docs/sql.md` (new paragraph in "Statements" documenting the FROM-less form, what's allowed/rejected, and the fail-closed column-reference behavior), `TODO.md` (this entry), `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`. No catalog/persistent-format/NSQL-wire/Raft change — this is pure parser+executor scalar-evaluation surface, the same "no format impact" class as `EXPLAIN`/`ANALYZE`. 117. [x] **Spatial track — SRID-argument out-of-range values silently truncated instead of rejected (6 call sites)** (2026-09-04). Continuing on log #115 (two predicate bugs) after the user said "fix all bugs" a second time — read the same way as log #115's own framing: a fresh bug-hunt pass on the Spatial/Collections code, not a re-litigation of anything already closed. Prompted by testing the newly-landed FROM-less `SELECT` (log #116) against spatial functions as an interaction check (`SELECT ST_Point(1,2,99999)`) — that specific query was not itself the bug (the raw evaluator `eval.go` dispatches to `evalSpatialFn`/`evalCollectionFn` purely by function name with no binder dependency, so it behaves identically reached via the NoFrom bypass or the normal binder-validated path — confirmed by reading `eval.go`, not assumed), but running it surfaced a real, pre-existing defect. **Bug**: `sql/parser.geoTypeArgs` (the `GEOMETRY(sub, srid)` DDL form) already validates a declared SRID fits a `u16`, erroring `"SRID out of range"` for anything `> 0xFFFF` — but six other places that accept a caller-supplied SRID skipped that check and instead did a bare `uint16(n)` narrowing conversion, which Go silently wraps (`99999 -> 34463`) rather than erroring: `ST_Point`'s 3rd (SRID) argument, `ST_SetSRID`'s 2nd argument, `ST_Transform`'s target-SRID argument, `ST_GeomFromGeoJSON`'s 2nd argument (all four in `internal/executor/eval_spatial.go`), and the EWKT text prefix `"SRID=<n>;..."` parsed by `types.ParseGeneralWKT` (`internal/sql/types/spatial.go`), which read `n` with `strconv.ParseUint(..., 32)` — valid for a `u32` but not the `u16` a column's SRID actually is, so the same wraparound happened one call-site downstream instead, in whichever caller later narrowed `g.SRID` into a destination column's `Type.Precision`. Net effect: `ST_Point(-73.98, 40.75, 99999)` or `ST_GeomFromText('SRID=99999;POINT(1 2)')` silently produced a geometry tagged SRID 34463 with no error — a correctness violation (CLAUDE.md priority #1) masquerading as success; confirmed live (`ST_SRID(ST_GeomFromText('SRID=99999;POINT(1 2)'))` returned `34463`, not an error) before fixing. **Fix**: new shared `asSRID(v types.Value) (uint16, error)` helper in `eval_spatial.go` — coerces to `Int64`, rejects `< 0 || > 0xFFFF` with the exact same `"SRID out of range"` message `geoTypeArgs` uses, wired into all four `eval_spatial.go` call sites in place of the bare `Coerce`+`uint16()` pattern; `ParseGeneralWKT`'s EWKT-prefix parse changed from `strconv.ParseUint(..., 10, 32)` to `strconv.ParseUint(..., 10, 16)` (which itself returns `ErrRange` for an out-of-range value, mapped to the same `"SRID out of range"` message) so the text-prefix path fails at the same point the DDL path does rather than one hop downstream. Re-verified live after the fix: all six sites now return `"nextsql: nextsql invalid_argument: nextsql: SRID out of range"`; the max valid value (65535) and a normal one (4326/3857) still work; negative input (`-1`) also correctly rejected (was wrapping to 65535 before). **Tests**: `internal/sql/types/spatial_test.go` — `TestSpatialEWKTPrefixSRIDRange` (rejects 99999, accepts the 65535 boundary); `internal/executor/spatial_test.go` — `TestSpatialSRIDArgRange` (table-driven: all 6 bad-input call sites error, boundary + normal values still resolve to the right `ST_SRID`). **Also checked and found clean, no fix needed**: all 5 driver implementations (Python/PHP/JS-family's EWKB *decoders* just read whatever `u32` SRID the server encoded — nothing to narrow client-side; their *encoders* only build an `"SRID=<n>;<wkt>"` string and send it as a param, so they're protected transitively by the server-side `ParseGeneralWKT` fix with no separate client-side check needed, matching this engine's "server is the single source of truth for validation" precedent) — confirmed by reading, not assumed. **Also confirmed clean this pass**: the live end-to-end Node-driver "whole collection/geometry column value" query that looked broken at the end of the prior "fix it" round turned out to be a bug in the throwaway test script itself (called `conn.query()`, which returns a streaming `Rows` iterator by design, instead of `conn.exec()`, which collects to `{columns, rows, affected}`) — not a driver or server defect; re-verified with `conn.exec()` that STRUCT/ARRAY/MAP/GEOMETRY/GEOGRAPHY whole-value decoding is correct end to end over the live wire (recorded in this session's project-state memory so a future live-check script doesn't waste time on the same false lead). **Verify**: `go build ./...` clean; `go test ./internal/sql/types/... ./internal/executor/...` green (incl. `aggregate`/`join`/`sort`/`vector` subpackages, ~70s); live-verified against a real `nextsqld` binary for every fixed call site plus the boundary/normal-value cases. **Docs**: `TODO.md` (this entry); no `docs/design-spatial.md`/`docs/sql.md` change needed — the documented behavior (SRID is a u16, out-of-range values are rejected) was already correct, only the code's enforcement of it was incomplete. No catalog/persistent-format/NSQL-wire change — pure input-validation fix in already-landed evaluator code. Everything uncommitted, per the standing repo convention. **Concurrent sessions**: `ListAgents` checked before and after this entry was appended (`nextsql-0a` still active on log #116's follow-on work; a new `nextsql-fb` session started mid-pass, not yet touched anything in this area) — only files touched this pass (`internal/executor/eval_spatial.go`+`spatial_test.go`, `internal/sql/types/spatial.go`+`spatial_test.go`, `TODO.md`) confirmed disjoint from both peers' known work before appending.

Wired by `cmd/nextsqld/main.go` alongside the audit log's own pre-existing open/signing-keyset setup, reusing the already-resolved `audit`/`auditSigningKeys` locals (no new state); a file-open/read failure (e.g. removed out from under a running server) is folded into the same `TailReport` shape via `Problem` — real operational information, not silently degraded to "not attached," distinguishable by an admin session as `problem` non-empty despite `lines=0`. Direct continuation of log #129 under the same "must be all status is landed" directive — M9's second of three pieces. `nextsqld` logs to stderr (JSON `slog`) and, under a service manager, to the journal; a driver-only Manager can reach neither, the same shape of gap M5 and M4's TLS/key/audit surfaces each hit. **What landed**: new `internal/logging.Ring` — a fixed-capacity (`DefaultRingCapacity` = 500), oldest-evicted-first buffer with O(1) amortized push and a `Snapshot(max)` that returns the newest `max` records oldest-first; memory is bounded by capacity regardless of process lifetime or log volume (same resource-safety property as `security.eventRing` from #128). 133. [x] **Phase 28 twenty-second increment — Manager MVP slice M5: Backups, completing the Manager MVP** (2026-09-04). Final slice under "must be all status is landed". M5 was found blocked twice (logs #123, #128) on "no `system.*` surface, the CLI is file-based" — but this time the investigation found a **real technical core**, not just a missing surface: `backup.Create` does its own `storage.Open` → checkpoint → close → copy, and WAL open **truncates a torn tail** (`wal.truncateSeg`), so a second engine open inside a running nextsqld — or `nextsql backup` against a live server under write load — can truncate a WAL segment the live engine is mid-write on. A quiet test of `nextsql backup` against a running server "passes" only because nothing was writing during the backup window; that is a latent footgun in the existing CLI, out of scope here. **What landed**: new `backup.CreateFromEngine(LiveEngine, dataDir, dest, keys, opt)` — `Create`'s post-checkpoint body factored into a shared `writeBackup`, and `CreateFromEngine` takes the server's **already-open** engine (checkpoint it, read `CheckpointLSN`/`RedoLSN`/`DurableLSN`, copy the file set). No second `storage.Open`, no second recovery, so neither pass can truncate the other's WAL tail. The copy is a fuzzy snapshot restore reconciles by replaying WAL from `RedoLSN` (the standard hot-backup model), and the restore-test still gates publication. New config key `backup_dir`. **New `BACKUP DATABASE` and `VERIFY BACKUP 'name'` statements** (`internal/sql`): `BACKUP` is *already* a lexer keyword (it names the `BACKUP` privilege in `GRANT`) so `BACKUP DATABASE` dispatches from the top-level switch; `VERIFY` is matched as a bare identifier (like #132's `config`), so nothing named `verify` breaks and `SELECT … FROM system.backups` is unaffected. `ast.BackupDatabase{}` / `ast.VerifyBackup{Name}`, dispatched in `session.go` before the binder; `authorize` accepts the existing `PrivBackup`/`ScopeDatabase` **or** `PrivAdmin`/`ScopeCluster` (a dedicated backup privilege already existed — no need to require full cluster admin); node-local, `BACKUP DATABASE` rejected inside a transaction; audited `security.ActionBackup` / new `security.ActionBackupVerify`. 135. [x] **Phase 28 twenty-fourth increment — GUI installer M1: architecture decision + serving backbone + the full working wizard flow** (2026-09-04). Direct continuation after log #134's packaging verification. First resolved the open architecture question via `AskUserQuestion` (recorded in `docs/design-installer-gui.md` §1): a small Go binary (`nextsql-install`) opening a loopback HTTP server with an embedded wizard UI and launching the operator's system browser to it — the same pattern already chosen for NextSQL Manager, over a native Go GUI toolkit (Wails/Fyne), three separate per-OS native installers, or a terminal-UI-first wizard — for the same reasons (smallest attack surface, one static binary per OS, real-browser accessibility for free). **The load-bearing design choice**: the installer never links the storage engine, `internal/crypto`, `internal/setup`, or `internal/sysinfo` at all (enforced by a new `imports_test.go`, mirroring Manager's own engine-import boundary test) — every effect happens by shelling out to the already-built, already-tested `nextsql` binary (`nextsql setup --dry-run --json` for live, side-effect-free preview on every screen up to Summary; `nextsql setup --json`, no `--dry-run`, for the one mutating call). A bug in the HTTP/JS layer therefore cannot reach key material in-process, because that process never holds any. The root password crosses the loopback boundary exactly once: the browser posts it to `nextsql-install`'s own local API, which writes it to a mode-0600 temp file for the single subprocess invocation and deletes it immediately after — the same `--password-file` contract every other NextSQL surface already uses (never argv, which `ps` would leak; never a URL). Auth is a single-run random 256-bit token embedded in the URL (`?token=…`, Jupyter-style) plus a cookie and an `X-Installer-Token` header on every `/api/*` call — deliberately not a login screen, since there is nothing to authenticate against before the first database exists; same CSP/security-header posture as Manager (`default-src 'self'`, no inline script, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`). **What landed**: new `cmd/nextsql-install` binary + `internal/installgui` package serving an embedded wizard — Welcome → Location (data dir/key file, live capacity/permission feedback via `--dry-run`, hardware detection surfaced) → Resources (Balanced/Memory Conservative/High Performance/Custom presets with a live buffer-pool preview) → Administrator (account creation, client-side strength hint, show/hide toggle, mismatch/minimum-length gate) → Summary (renders every field the mutating call will use, built from the exact same `Params` the dry-run used) → Install (the one mutating `/api/v1/install` call, transactional rollback on failure via `nextsql setup`'s pre-existing rollback — logs #106–#108, #110 — so a failed GUI install behaves identically to a failed CLI one) → Completion (the `nextsqld` command to run next, or the `--config-in` command for a skip-init install; never echoes the password). New `internal/browseropen` package, extracted from `internal/oidcclient`'s pre-existing `DefaultBrowserOpener` (now a thin wrapper over it) so the installer and the OIDC login flow share one cross-platform "open a browser" implementation rather than duplicating it. `nextsql-install`'s own request log records only method/path/status/duration — never a request body, the token, or subprocess stdout/stderr — closing the "protected installer logs with secret redaction" checklist line. **Tests**: `internal/installgui`'s new `defaults_test.go`/`imports_test.go`/`params_test.go`/`runner_test.go`/`server_test.go` (token auth accept/reject, `Params.Validate`/`toArgs`, the engine-import boundary, default-path detection, the runner's password-file-lifecycle and rollback-surfacing behavior, API handler shapes). **Live-verified end to end** against real binaries (job scratch dir, cleaned up after): the full API sequence `/api/v1/hello` → `/api/v1/plan` (dry-run, writes nothing) → `/api/v1/install` (real `nextsql init` + admin account + health check) produced a working, health-verified database; connected with a real `nextsql exec` as the admin account the wizard created and got a real query result back. **Docs**: new `docs/design-installer-gui.md` (architecture rationale, milestone table, API surface, non-goals), `TODO.md` (installer-UX checklist: hardware detection, resource presets, install summary, rollback, never-delete-on-failure, health verification, completion screen, no-secrets-in-connection-strings, protected logs all checked with GUI scope noted; "Automation parity" line updated), `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`. Not yet done, deliberately scoped out of M1 and tracked as M2–M5: recovery-key export, the generate-vs-import key disclosure, a TLS certificate assistant/remote-listen flow, bundling `nextsql-install` into the OS packaging artifacts, and an accessibility/theming pass.

139. [x] **Phase 28 twenty-eighth increment — GUI installer M6 complete: service registration / start at boot** (2026-09-04). Direct continuation after log #138. `PROJECT.md` §46 lists "service registration" as intended installer scope. Two designs were weighed: have the wizard *author* a systemd unit file itself, or have it only *enable* a unit some packaged installer (`.deb`/`.tar.gz`/`.run`) already placed on disk. **Chosen: enable-only.** Authoring unit files (root-vs-user paths, templating `ExecStart`/`ConditionPathExists` to match wherever the operator put the binaries) is exactly what `packaging/linux/{nextsql.service,nextsql.user.service}` and `tarball/install.sh` already do correctly today; duplicating that logic in the GUI installer risks the two definitions drifting apart, and a from-source `nextsql-install` run (no packaging involved at all) has nowhere authoritative to copy a unit's `ExecStart` paths from. **What landed**: new `internal/installgui/service.go` — the only other place besides `nextsql setup` this package shells out from (documented as such in the package doc comment). `DetectService` is read-only (`systemctl cat`/`is-enabled`/`is-active` for a "nextsql" unit, scoped `--user` unless running as root, same split `detectDefaults` already uses) and never errors on "not found"/"no systemd here" — both expected states. New `GET /api/v1/service` exposes it to the wizard; new `Params.EnableService`; a new `maybeEnableService` (server.go) calls the one mutating function, `EnableService` (`systemctl enable --now nextsql`), only after independently re-verifying the just-initialized database is health-verified OK, a "nextsql" unit exists in this operator's own scope, and that unit's own `ExecStart --config` (parsed from `systemctl cat`) already equals the config path `nextsql setup` just wrote — never a unit it has to guess about. Any refusal is a clear, non-fatal reason; it never flips an already-succeeded database install to a failure. **A real bug found and fixed during live verification, not assumed away**: `systemctl enable --now` exits `0` once a start has been *issued*, even for a unit whose process exits immediately after — reproduced live by installing without a bootstrap admin user, which makes a genuinely started `nextsqld` immediately refuse to run and exit, while `enable --now` itself still reported success. Fixed with a separate `Active` field: after `EnableService` succeeds, a bounded `WaitActive` polls `systemctl is-active` up to 4 times over ~1.5s (enough grace for WAL recovery/catalog decode on a real start, never unbounded) before concluding it did not stay running; the completion screen and docs distinguish "enabled to start at boot" from "actually running now" accordingly. **Tests**: `service_test.go` (`execStartConfigRe` parsing, `systemctlArgs` scope handling, a real-host `DetectService`/`EnableService` pair that only ever probes read-only or fails cleanly against a nonexistent unit name); `server_test.go` (`GET /api/v1/service` shape; install with `enableService:true` against a host with no matching unit → the database install still succeeds with a clear non-fatal `service.error`; install without `enableService` → no `service` field at all). **Live-verified end to end** against a real *user-scope* systemd unit registered for this exact purpose (`systemctl --user`, no root, fully disabled/removed/`daemon-reload`d afterward, confirmed gone): `GET /api/v1/service` correctly found it and parsed its `--config` path; a real install without an admin user + `enableService:true` produced `{"enabled":true,"active":false}` with the accurate reason (the live-reproduced bug above); a second real install *with* an admin user produced `{"enabled":true,"active":true}`, independently confirmed via `systemctl --user is-active`/`is-enabled`, and a real `nextsql exec … SELECT 1` succeeded against the systemd-managed `nextsqld`. **Docs**: `docs/design-installer-gui.md` (M6 complete section), `TODO.md` (checklist line + milestone table + header table + "Last updated" + this entry), `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`. **M6 is now COMPLETE.** Open Phase 28 GUI-installer work: M2's recovery-key export/verification, M4 (packaging integration — bundling `nextsql-install` into the `.tar.gz`/`.run`/`.deb`/`.msi`/`.pkg` artifacts as the default interactive entry point), M5 (accessibility pass + theming), and the installer exit gate's remaining end-to-end items (Windows install, silent install, upgrade/repair through the installer path specifically, accessibility baseline).

**Note on logs #134–#139**: these six increments' code, tests, and doc updates (`docs/design-installer-gui.md`, the `TODO.md` checklist boxes, `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`) were already landed in the working tree, but the corresponding numbered log entries here were missed at the time — a real documentation-discipline gap, not a fabrication: every claim above is reconstructed from what is actually in the tree (shipped code, passing tests recorded in `CHANGELOG.md`, and `docs/design-installer-gui.md`'s own contemporaneous landing writeups), not invented after the fact. Found and fixed while resuming work per "continue @TODO.md" (2026-09-04) — `TODO.md`'s own rule ("do not silently reconcile contradictions — fix the docs or report the conflict") applies to gaps in this file's own log just as much as to disagreements between files.

142. [x] **NextSQL Installer + NextSQL Manager + NextSQL Studio merged into one product, NextSQL Admin** (2026-09-05). User directive: "NextSQL Installer, NextSQL Studio, NextSQL Manager turns into single NextSQL Admin" — clarified via `AskUserQuestion` as a full architectural merge (one binary/shell, not a rename), applied now as a restructuring of the already-landed Installer/Manager work, covering both docs and code. Studio (Phase 29) is still 0% built, so "merge" for it meant reserving its place in the unified shell rather than implementing its ~140-item feature checklist.

**Target architecture**: one binary `cmd/nextsql-admin`, package `internal/admin`, three modes — `internal/admin/setup` (formerly `internal/installgui`, unchanged behavior: single-operator token loopback auth, drives `nextsql setup` as a subprocess), `internal/admin/ops` (formerly `internal/manager`, unchanged behavior: operator NSQL-credential session + CSRF, the nine `system.*` read-model/action views), `internal/admin/studio` (new, placeholder only — no logic). Setup and Operations are sequential lifecycle phases of the same install, never concurrent, so `nextsql-admin` picks exactly one mode at startup by shelling out to the existing `nextsql lifecycle detect --json` (no new CLI surface): no initialized installation → Setup mode (ephemeral port, auto-open browser, token auth); an initialized one → Operations mode (fixed `127.0.0.1:7220` default, login required). A `--mode setup|operate` flag overrides detection. New unauthenticated `GET /api/v1/mode` (`{"mode":"setup"|"operate"}`) is the one endpoint that exists before either sub-app's own auth applies — the frontend's first call, deciding which sub-app to mount.
